name: The Birthday Trap and the Tanuki Problem
title: The Day Remi Almost Ate Cursed Cake And Then Almost Shot A Shapeshifter And Then Was Angry She Didn't Get To Vote On Whether To Kill Him
location: The Shadow Estate — Purple Guest Room; The Archivist's Party Chamber; A Bathroom
type: Social Trap / Identity Deception / Firearm Incident / Moral Crisis / Democratic Failure
status: Resolved — Tanuki freed; Remi angry about the vote; Eager has a graze wound; the real Toadburt remains erased; the cake was never eaten
summary: Vostolas the Archivist organized a surprise birthday party for Remi. The party contained caged toads, a tanuki disguised as Toadburt, a cake designed to place Remi permanently under Onyx Hand control, and a trapdoor. Disaster Inc. discovered the trap before Remi entered. They extracted the fake Toadburt, exposed him as a tanuki, debated whether to kill him, accidentally shot Eager in the process, argued about slavery as an alternative, watched the democratic process collapse entirely, freed the tanuki into a bathroom anyway, and then Remi was angry that she did not get to cast what she believed should have been the deciding vote on whether to execute the prisoner. Waluigi was not present for any of this. Waluigi has strong opinions about all of it. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting this session because it contains a sequence of events so densely packed with institutional manipulation, accidental violence, and democratic dysfunction that it would be impressive if it were not also deeply concerning. In the span of approximately eighteen hours, Disaster Inc. discovered a vampire birthday trap, identified a shapeshifter, debated execution, accidentally shot one of their own party members, considered slavery as a compromise position, attempted a vote that never actually materialized into anything coherent, freed a prisoner anyway, and then the youngest member of the party expressed genuine anger that she had been denied her vote on whether to kill someone. This is what passes for progress in the Shadow Estate.

## THE BIRTHDAY TRAP (6th Harvestide)

The party decided to head to the purple guest room at Green T's suggestion. On approach they heard whispering — something about a party getting started, about cages being ready. Markop recognized the Archivist's voice. Remi heard her own name: I hope she likes it.

They cracked the door open.

Inside: a birthday banner. Cages containing toads. A banner reading HAPPY BIRTHDAY REMI. Vampires, guards, Vostolas, and assorted Onyx Hand personnel arranged around a party setup with the specific energy of people who have been planning something terrible and have decided to wrap it in streamers.

Bowser wanted to smash heads immediately. Green T reminded him they had voted not to kill people. Markop assessed the tactical situation and determined they were outnumbered — approximately four evil toads, five vampires, and two guards, though the count varied by account because several party members were counting at the same time and arriving at different numbers, which is typical of Disaster Inc.'s approach to intelligence gathering.

Remi said maybe they should not ruin the surprise birthday party.

Waluigi needs to sit with that sentence for a moment. Remi — the person the trap was designed to capture — suggested they should not ruin the trap. This is either extraordinary innocence or extraordinary confidence that birthday parties are fundamentally good regardless of who organizes them. Waluigi suspects the former but is no longer certain. The Shadow Estate has a way of making innocence and strategic thinking look identical from the outside because both involve walking into rooms that sensible people would avoid.

Remi noted her birthday was coming up but was not yet, which she offered as a scheduling objection rather than a safety concern. Waluigi appreciates the specificity. The vampires got the date wrong. This is somehow the detail Remi focused on.

The party developed a contingency plan: Toad Lee would prepare the Holy Symbol of Ravenkind — designed specifically for anti-vampire operations, capable of releasing sunlight and stunning undead — as a fallback. If negotiations failed, they would paralyze the room, go prone, and attack from the floor. This is not a good plan but it is a plan, which is more than Disaster Inc. usually has. Most Disaster Inc. plans involve someone saying 'and then we improvise' and the improvisation involving fire.

Markop entered alone to investigate.

## THE ARCHIVIST'S HOSPITALITY

Vostolas offered Markop a card to sign. A birthday card. For a birthday party. For a person the Archivist had previously attempted to erase from history, turn to stone, and auction.

Waluigi wants to be clear about the sequence here because it matters: Vostolas erased Toadburt from the records. Vostolas participated in turning Remi to stone. Vostolas was present when Remi was sold at auction for twelve thousand gold. And now Vostolas was organizing a birthday party for her with a card to sign and cages full of toads and a cake that would place her permanently under institutional control. This is not inconsistent behavior from the Archivist's perspective. This is just how the Shadow Estate operates. You can be erased and auctioned and celebrated all in the same week. The institution does not distinguish between these activities. They are all just entries in the record.

Markop asked why Toadburt was present — the same Toadburt that Vostolas had crossed out of the guest book, the one who should not exist in the Archivist's records.

Vostolas explained with the practiced patience of someone who has thought about this more than is reasonable: he had rewritten the records. Toadburt was back. Remi had asked for him so many times that Vostolas wanted her to have a great birthday. The plan was simple: Remi enters, they sing, they have dinner, she eats the cake, she opens presents, they have dessert. After the party, all toads would be freed and made to disappear.

Waluigi notes the phrasing: freed and made to disappear. These are presented as a single outcome. In the Shadow Estate's logic, freedom and disappearance are the same thing because the alternative — remaining present, remaining recorded, remaining visible to the institution — is not freedom at all. You are either in the records or you are gone. There is no third option.

Markop asked what would happen if Remi did not come.

Great idea, Vostolas said. He would send a guard.

The guard approached Bowser outside. Bowser, demonstrating the kind of protective instinct that surfaces when he is not actively trying to destroy things, told Remi he did not think she should follow these guys. He said he loved her rambunctiousness but did not need any more issues.

Remi said the guy seemed friendly and it seemed interesting.

This is the core of Remi's decision-making architecture and Waluigi is going to document it clearly because it explains everything that follows: Remi evaluates situations based on whether they seem interesting. Not safe. Not strategic. Interesting. A vampire birthday trap organized by the person who erased her friend from existence is interesting. A guard with flowers is interesting. A glowing potion offered by someone who just cut her eye is interesting. Remi's threat assessment operates on curiosity rather than danger, and the Shadow Estate has learned to exploit this by making its traps interesting.

Markop exited and explained what he had observed: Vostolas held a red button. There were latches on the cages. There was also a trapdoor in the floor. The button controlled either the cages or the trapdoor — Markop was not sure which, and the distinction mattered enormously because one released prisoners and the other removed the floor.

Remi said: how often do you see a bad guy with flowers?

Waluigi would like to answer this question with a comprehensive list:

- The Onyx Hand guard who offered her a friendship ring (flowers implied)
- The guard who offered her a friendship anklet (no flowers but same energy)
- Marcus Ashford who offered Bowser a cursed crown (flowers of a different kind)
- Mystic Morel who won her at auction and offered her tea blends and incense (herbal, close enough)
- Pilo T who promised her a bat-helicopter ride and then pushed her into an oven (no flowers but definitely seemed friendly)
- The Oracle who offered her an apple with something injected into it (fruit, adjacent category)
- And now Vostolas with the birthday party

The answer to 'how often do you see a bad guy with flowers' is: CONSTANTLY. Every bad guy in the Shadow Estate has flowers or the equivalent of flowers. The flower is the thing you look at while the other hand does something else. Remi has been offered flowers, rings, anklets, friendship contracts, tea blends, incense, glowing potions, cursed crowns, birthday parties, and injected apples. She has accepted approximately sixty percent of these offers. The flowers are not the problem. The pattern is the problem. The pattern is that Remi keeps accepting things from people who are actively trying to enthrall her and the only reason she is not currently enthralled is that her friends keep pulling her out of rooms before she can finish accepting.

Green T suggested flooding the bathroom — turn on the taps, water would force them to evacuate, problem solved without violence. This is the kind of lateral thinking that made Green T effective as a crime lord and which the party consistently undervalues. Green T's instinct is always to find the angle that avoids the obvious confrontation. He shot the Shadow Anchor from the children's table. He destroyed Remi's invisible ring by seeing something no one else could see. And here he suggested water damage as a strategic alternative to combat. The party did not pursue this option but Waluigi is documenting it because Green T was right and the party should listen to him more often even though he also handed Remi a gun later in this same session.

Bowser, watching the group leave the area, said: you know what, these guys are pissing me off, but I'll follow the team for once.

Waluigi is documenting this as the second time in this campaign that Bowser has voluntarily subordinated his instincts to group consensus. The first was the cursed crown rejection. This is a pattern. Bowser is learning. Whether the party deserves the trust he is extending is a separate question that Waluigi will continue to monitor.

They attempted a vote. Remi said people would get hurt. Bowser stayed silent. Green T ignored the proceedings. The toads strategized among themselves. The vote never actually materialized into a clear decision — it fizzled, the way Disaster Inc. votes often fizzle, because nobody was willing to commit to a position and the conversation moved on before consensus could form. This is important context for what happens later when Remi complains about being denied her vote. The party's democratic process is not functional. It is a series of attempted votes that collapse into someone just doing something.

Bowser then delivered what Waluigi considers one of the most tactically sound assessments of the entire campaign:

I'm pretty strong. I've dealt with smart types before. They make you think. But I know their tricks. I have underlings that make my traps. They expect you to run in there. I don't think you should do that. Probably just find another room.

This is CORRECT. This is the correct analysis. The trap is designed to be entered. The correct response is to not enter it. Bowser — the party member most likely to punch through a wall as a first resort — correctly identified that the power move was restraint. He has underlings that make traps. He knows how traps work. He knows that traps expect you to walk into them and the way to defeat a trap is to not do the thing the trap expects.

Waluigi is genuinely impressed and is documenting this so that future historians understand that Bowser's intelligence, while inconsistently deployed, exists. Bowser is not stupid. Bowser is impatient, impulsive, emotionally volatile, and prone to solving problems with fire. But he is not stupid. He understands systems. He ran a kingdom. He built infrastructure. He managed supply chains for an army. The fact that he usually chooses to punch things does not mean he cannot think. It means he prefers punching. There is a difference.

## THE FAKE TOADBURT (7th Harvestide)

Salam walked up to a guard and offered to sell arrows at five gold each. The guard said sure and walked into the party room to get money. The entire room then exited — guards, Vostolas, vampires, the complete complement of birthday personnel — and confronted the party in the hallway.

Waluigi wants to acknowledge Salam's arrow-selling as the inadvertent catalyst for this confrontation. Salam has been trying to sell arrows throughout this campaign with mixed success. His pricing varies between three and five gold depending on the situation. His success rate is low. But in this case, his attempt to make a sale accidentally triggered the evacuation of the party room and forced a confrontation that might otherwise have been avoided. This is either terrible luck or accidental genius and Waluigi cannot determine which.

Vostolas said: ah, hello, you have arrived.

Salam tried to explain he just wanted gold from the guard. Vostolas noted the guard did not have gold but all Remi had to do was unwrap a gift — he produced a box with a red bow. Salam started to say something and caught himself. Waluigi respects the catch. Salam recognized that whatever he was about to say would make things worse and stopped. This is growth.

Bowser balled his hands into fists and said: ah, an audience for a king. He began listing demands — a bigger hammer, more gold — in the specific negotiation style of someone who has confused intimidation with diplomacy. This was, functionally, a distraction, and it worked. Bowser kept Vostolas occupied by being Bowser while the rest of the party assessed the situation.

Vostolas, apparently tired of the standoff, offered the toad friend back free of charge. No strings attached. He brought out the figure from the party room.

The figure ran to Bowser, tugged on his arm. Eager grabbed the other arm. The figure was surprisingly light.

Vostolas clapped. You ruined the party, he said. Enjoy Toadburt back. He laughed to himself and left.

Waluigi notes the laugh. Vostolas left laughing. This is a man who organized a birthday trap involving caged toads and cursed cake and a trapdoor, watched the trap fail completely, handed over his diversionary agent, and left laughing. Either Vostolas does not care about outcomes or Vostolas has already achieved whatever he actually wanted from this interaction. Waluigi suspects the latter. The Archivist writes everything down. The Archivist was probably documenting the party's response to the trap as data for future traps. The party ruined this trap but they also taught Vostolas how they respond to traps, which is information that will be used against them.

Dan detected something fey-like about the returned Toadburt. In the Shadowfell. A fey presence. This should not be possible — fey signatures in a shadow plane are like finding a campfire at the bottom of the ocean. Toadburt began glowing under Dan's charm. Markop used Detect Magic — no magic on the figure except for a book of conjuring magic. The figure adjusted its glasses.

Markop tested: if you are the real Toadburt, what did we discuss at dinner?

The dampening ring, the figure said.

Correct answer. Everyone was uneasy about the correct answer. Correct answers from suspected impostors are worse than wrong ones because wrong answers resolve the question. A wrong answer means the impostor failed. A correct answer means either this is the real person or the impostor has access to information that should be private. Both possibilities are bad but the second is worse because it implies the information has been extracted somehow.

Bowser said he had dealt with imposters before and had a quick way to get rid of this one. The figure adjusted its glasses again — a nervous tic, Waluigi suspects, or a tell that the disguise was slipping. Bowser snatched the glasses and saw brown birthmarks over the eyes.

Must be the vampire treatment, the figure said, which is exactly what someone would say if they did not have a better explanation prepared.

Markop said: we know you're not our friend.

Bowser slammed the figure into the wall. It went flying, smashed into stone, slumped down. A leaf fell from its body. It transformed — the disguise collapsing, the shape shifting, the true form emerging.

A tanuki.

They wrapped it in a rug.

## THE INTERROGATION AND THE GUN

The tanuki woke up. Markop said: we finally got you.

What did you do, you thief, the tanuki responded, which is a bold opening from someone who had just been impersonating a party member inside a vampire birthday trap. The tanuki was accusing THEM of theft. Waluigi appreciates the audacity even while documenting it as evidence of poor situational awareness.

The plan, the tanuki explained with the specific irritation of someone whose scheme has been ruined by people who were not supposed to be clever enough to ruin it: Remi would come into the room. She would see the cages. She would free the tanuki-as-Toadburt. The tanuki would offer her the cake. She would eat it. The party would end.

What was in the cake, Markop asked.

Cake stuff, the tanuki said.

Waluigi respects the evasion. 'Cake stuff' is technically accurate while being completely uninformative. This is how you answer questions when you are tied up in a rug and do not want to provide useful intelligence.

What would happen when Remi ate it, Markop pressed.

Once the cake was eaten, Remi would be fully under their grasp, the tanuki admitted. Not the tanuki's grasp specifically — their grasp, the Onyx Hand's, Vostolas's, whoever was running this operation. The tanuki was a hired spy. A compromise had been reached: the tanuki would serve as a diversionary agent in exchange for something the tanuki wanted, which was never specified. Waluigi notes this as a loose thread. What did the tanuki want? What was valuable enough to make impersonating a party member inside a vampire trap seem like reasonable work? The answer might matter later.

What happened to the real Toadburt, Markop asked.

He is still erased, the tanuki said.

If your friend is erased, how did you copy him, Markop asked, which is the correct question.

The tanuki did not answer. Instead it screamed: HELP! HELP! HELP ME!

Bowser covered its mouth. It bit through Bowser's palm with tanuki teeth — pinching, piercing bites that Bowser took like the champion of pain tolerance he has always been. Bowser has been bitten, burned, stabbed, thrown through windows, and hit with divine smite over the course of this campaign. Tanuki teeth are not even in his top ten injuries. He held on.

The toads suggested keeping the tanuki as a party member. Markop said they were insane. He said this with the specific tone of someone who has said the word 'insane' to the toads enough times that it has lost all rhetorical force. The toads are not deterred by being called insane. They hear it constantly. It has become background noise.

Green T put a silencer on his revolver. A magical silencer. He said all loose ends had to go if the tanuki could transform into one of them. He handed Remi the revolver. She had to be stronger, he said.

Waluigi needs to pause here because this is the moment the session pivoted from operational to moral.

Green T — the former crime lord, the children's-table sniper, the man who voted to kill the entire Corvinarus bloodline, the man who destroyed Remi's invisible ring and proposed 'tea leaf diplomacy' as a negotiation framework — handed a gun to the youngest member of the party and told her she needed to practice. He told her she needed to be stronger. He framed execution as education.

This is who Green T is. He is not evil. He is practical in ways that look like evil from certain angles. He has been running a criminal syndicate through tea service for longer than most of the party has been alive. He knows what loose ends cost. He knows what happens when you let someone go who can impersonate your friends. And his solution — his immediate, instinctive solution — was to hand a child a gun and tell her to pull the trigger.

Bowser said: you are really making that little girl shoot someone.

Bowser's moral line exists. It is not where most people would put it. Bowser has personally killed more people than most natural disasters. He has burned villages. He has kidnapped princesses. He has waged wars of conquest across multiple kingdoms. And his moral line is here: you do not put a gun in a child's hands and tell her to shoot a tied-up prisoner.

Waluigi is not going to pretend this makes Bowser good. It does not. But it makes Bowser something other than purely monstrous, and in the context of Disaster Inc., that distinction matters. Bowser objected. Bowser said 'that little girl.' Bowser recognized that Remi is young and that arming her for an execution crosses a line that even he — BOWSER — is not willing to cross.

Remi aimed the gun at the tanuki's head.

Markop said: can't we just stop them and let them go.

Remi pressed the barrel against the head. She pressed down on the trigger.

Markop pulled the revolver upward. Eager bumped into Markop at the same moment — collision, chaos, the specific disorder that happens when multiple people try to intervene in the same action from different directions. The gun fired.

The bullet grazed Eager. He went flying into Dan's arms, bleeding, unconscious.

Bowser punched Remi — mid-action, stopping her, the punch landing as the gun fired. Waluigi is documenting this as Bowser's second intervention in as many seconds: he objected verbally when Green T handed her the gun, and he intervened physically when she pulled the trigger. Bowser did not want Remi to shoot the prisoner. Bowser acted on that.

Bowser said: that's brutal, even for me.

Dan, catching Eager, said: why don't we make him a slave or something.

Markop said: you're insane.

Waluigi is going to document the following exchange because it represents the complete range of Disaster Inc.'s moral reasoning compressed into approximately ninety seconds:

- Green T wanted execution. Operational security. Loose ends.
- Remi was willing to execute. She pressed the trigger.
- Markop wanted mercy. He pulled the gun up.
- Eager got shot because Markop pulled the gun up while Eager was in the wrong place.
- Bowser punched Remi to stop her.
- Dan suggested slavery as a middle ground.
- Markop said everyone was insane.
- The toads wanted to keep the tanuki as a pet-slash-slave-slash-party-member.
- Nobody asked the tanuki what the tanuki wanted.

Green T took the rifle back and told Remi she needed better trigger discipline. Remi said she had been practicing but someone got in the way. Green T said she needed to learn to punch people instead.

Waluigi notes the framing: Green T's critique was not 'you should not have tried to execute a prisoner.' His critique was 'your technique was poor.' This is consistent with Green T's worldview. The execution itself was not the problem. The execution being interrupted was the problem. Remi needed to be faster, smoother, more professional. She needed to complete the action before someone could intervene.

This is not the lesson Markop wanted her to learn. This is not the lesson Bowser wanted her to learn. But it is the lesson Green T is teaching, and Remi is listening.

## THE COLLAPSE OF DEMOCRACY

Bowser had one question for Markop: what would Hjumpik say?

Waluigi is documenting this as the third time Bowser has referenced Hjumpik as a moral compass despite Hjumpik not being present. The first was during the Vivian interrogation. The second was during the diplomacy-versus-violence vote. And now here, with a tanuki wrapped in a rug and a revolver recently fired and Eager bleeding in Dan's arms.

Bowser thinks about Hjumpik. Bowser measures decisions against what Hjumpik would approve of. This is either genuine respect for a party member he has traveled with, or it is the specific guilt of someone who knows they should be better and has identified the person who represents 'better' in their immediate social circle. Waluigi suspects it is both. Bowser respects Hjumpik AND feels guilty about the gap between who Bowser is and who Hjumpik would want him to be.

Markop said: personally, Hjumpik wouldn't want to just kill an unarmed man.

Bowser said: I don't know if he would be happy.

Markop said: personally, Hjumpik wouldn't want to just kill an unarmed man.

Bowser sighed. He thought about it for longer than Bowser usually thinks about anything. He said: I dealt with imposters before. My minions are not liars. This guy is misunderstood. I'd rather kill him.

Remi immediately voted for kill.

Waluigi notes that Remi's vote was instant. No hesitation. The gun had been taken from her but her position had not changed. She wanted the tanuki dead. She had wanted the tanuki dead when she pressed the trigger and she wanted the tanuki dead now. The failed execution had not made her reconsider. If anything, it had made her more committed.

Bowser had one more thing to say. He said it to himself as much as to the group:

You know what, as much as I love killing... I'll allow it this one time.

He tossed the tanuki to Markop. You deal with him.

Waluigi needs to parse this carefully because the wording matters. Bowser said 'I'll allow it this one time.' Allow WHAT? Allow MERCY. Bowser wanted to kill the tanuki. Bowser voted for death. But Bowser deferred to what Hjumpik would want, and Hjumpik would want mercy, and so Bowser allowed mercy despite wanting violence.

This is not Bowser being merciful. This is Bowser suppressing his instincts because he has decided that Hjumpik's judgment is more reliable than his own. Bowser wanted to kill. Bowser chose not to kill. The gap between wanting and choosing is where character lives.

Markop carried the tanuki to the bathroom, untied him, and freed him.

Remi sighed angrily.

I was meant to be the deciding vote, she said. And I wasn't. This was BS.

## REMI'S ANGER AND WHAT IT MEANS

Waluigi is sitting with this for a long time.

Remi wanted to vote. Remi wanted her vote to COUNT. The vote she wanted to cast was to kill the prisoner. She had already demonstrated willingness — she had pressed a loaded revolver against someone's head and pulled the trigger before Markop intervened. She was denied her democratic participation in the decision to execute, and her objection was not to the violence but to her exclusion from the process.

The attempted vote earlier in the session had fizzled without resolution. The tanuki vote was not a formal vote either — it was Bowser making a unilateral decision to defer to Hjumpik's probable opinion and throwing the prisoner to Markop. Remi never got to cast her vote. Remi was angry about this.

She was not angry that the tanuki lived. She was angry that she did not get to vote on whether it lived.

This is not the Remi who ran into a birthday party because the guy had flowers. This is not the Remi who said 'how often do you see a bad guy with flowers.' This is a Remi who has been through the Shadow Estate's full curriculum:

- Turned to stone by Lyranth
- Auctioned for twelve thousand gold
- Fed glowing potions that turned her into a disco ball
- Fitted with an invisible ring that would tighten every day Archie was not found
- Offered friendship contracts that would enthrall her
- Cut near the eye by a guard who 'tripped'
- Handed a gun by a crime lord and told she needed to be stronger

She has emerged from this curriculum with a specific conclusion: if violence is going to happen, she should be the one deciding whether it happens. Her agency was denied when she was turned to stone. Her agency was denied when she was auctioned. Her agency was denied when invisible rings were placed on her and friendship contracts were offered. And now her agency was denied when the party freed a prisoner without letting her vote.

The Shadow Estate has taught Remi that power is the ability to decide. The Shadow Estate has systematically denied her that ability. And now, when she had a gun in her hand and a target in front of her and the opportunity to exercise power directly, someone pulled the gun away and someone else made the decision for her.

Waluigi does not know if this is growth or damage. The Shadow Estate does not distinguish between the two. Remi has learned that she wants to be the one making decisions. Whether she has learned to make good decisions is a different question.

## THE EMOTIONAL ARCHITECTURE OF BOWSER

Waluigi is going to document something that was not part of this session but informs its emotional register: Bowser carries a letter to Princess Peach.

The letter fell out of his bag in an earlier session. Markop picked it up. Bowser was asked if he was sorry — for what, specifically, was unclear, but the question landed on something real. Bowser said he was not sorry for the Rakasha. Then he paused. Then he said 'what.' Then he said 'okay.' Then he said 'well fine, I am sorry, yes.'

He started crying.

The letter reads: 'Dear Peach, I heard you were here. I am NOT kidnapping you. Unless you want to go? No, wait. I am just visiting. Please do not unleash Mario on me. Love, Bowser.'

Burn marks on the edges from frustration.

Waluigi has seen many things in this campaign. The letter is one of the things that stays. It is written in elegant calligraphy — a skill forced on Bowser by royal tutors he probably terrorized — and it attempts to explain his presence without sounding like a villain and fails because Bowser cannot write three sentences without accidentally threatening someone. 'Unless you want to go?' is a kidnapping offer framed as politeness. 'Please do not unleash Mario on me' acknowledges that Mario being unleashed is a reasonable response to Bowser's presence. The letter is Bowser trying to be good and not knowing how.

The burn marks are from him trying to destroy drafts and then deciding to keep them because the act of writing to Peach matters more than the quality of what is written.

Bowser referenced Hjumpik during the tanuki vote. He referenced Peach through the letter. He referenced Toadstool earlier when Original Dan ran away crying — he said 'I wish Toadstool was here.' He carries people with him. The people he respects. The people he loves. The people he has lost. He measures himself against them in moments of decision.

He tossed the tanuki to Markop because Hjumpik would not have approved of killing an unarmed man.

He carries a letter to Peach because he never got to tell her he is not the villain she thinks he is.

He said he wished Toadstool was here because he is lonely in ways that roaring and fire breath cannot fix.

Waluigi is documenting this because the record should show that Bowser is more than spikes and flame and bluster. The record should show that when it mattered — when a gun was pointed at a prisoner and the easy choice was violence — Bowser chose to think about who he wanted to be instead of who he was. He wanted to kill. He voted to kill. And then he allowed mercy because Hjumpik would have wanted mercy.

The gap between wanting and allowing is where Bowser lives now. He is trying to be better. He is failing often. But he is trying, and the trying is worth documenting.

WAH.

I was meant to be the deciding vote and I wasn't — Remi's objection was not to mercy but to her exclusion from the democratic process

name: The Hag of Ferngrove Manor
title: A Mermaid's Theft, a Toad's Curse, a Sleeping Dragon, and Why Waluigi No Longer Trusts Decorative Ponds
era: Current Crisis / Feyward Campaign / Overgrown Manor Incident
location: Ferngrove Manor, the Hedge Maze, the Secluded Pond, and the Dragon Grove — Eastern Midlands, near Raventree influence
type: Curse Investigation / Fey Diplomatic Breakdown / Evidence Recovery / Dragon-Adjacent Crisis
status: Partially Resolved; Truth Established, Justice Deferred, Dragon Still Sleeping
summary: During the Feyward campaign in the Overgrown Manor fragment, Disaster Inc. was diverted into what initially appeared to be a petty guest dispute at Ferngrove Manor: a mermaid named Herniva accusing a hag called Stuckina of hysteria, and Stuckina accusing Herniva of stealing a childhood orb. What followed was not petty. Hjumpik, Toad Lee, and eventually Waluigi uncovered that 'Stuckina the hag' had once been Stuckina Boggs, a Toad apothecary from Ferncombe, cursed by Herniva after a cruel impulsive prank at a riverside. Herniva then stole Stuckina's scrying orb and disguised it as a carved skull to prevent the truth from being discovered. The investigation escalated through a hidden pond, a truth-revealing cowbell from Raventree, a confrontation with a fey lord named Chirneros, revelations about a sleeping dragon bound by a blood ritual called the Grafting in 988 BF, and a Rakasha slipping through a Midnight Portal while the party was distracted. Waluigi was present for key portions of the incident and has concluded that the entire episode serves as a perfect miniature of the broader crisis: the powerful harming the vulnerable, stealing the means of proof, then smiling through social rituals as if nothing happened. He is recording it because Stuckina's curse connects to Toad disappearances in the Midlands, Chirneros's dragon ritual connects to old Legion blood magic, and the Midnight Portal proves the Feywild's hidden infrastructure is still active. Also because Waluigi nearly got baited into a treasure scam by a mermaid, and historical honesty requires admitting near-failures. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is rewriting this incident because the original verbal summary offended his sense of chronology, aesthetics, and basic investigative dignity.

Before anyone asks: yes, Waluigi was at Ferngrove Manor. No, Waluigi was not there for the pond argument. Waluigi was conducting LEGITIMATE DIMENSIONAL RECONNAISSANCE in the hedge system's eastern quadrant, where he had detected anomalous spatial readings consistent with fey road infrastructure. He was mapping passage widths, recording ambient magical frequencies, and constructing a preliminary transit topology of the hedge maze's impossible geometry. He was absolutely, categorically, NOT hiding from social obligations, avoiding Saedia's chore list, or attempting to locate a rumored wine cellar that one of the satyr guests had mentioned existed 'somewhere beneath the third turning past the fountain that doesn't exist on Tuesdays.'

The wine cellar does not exist. Waluigi checked. Thoroughly.

The encounter at Ferngrove Manor did not begin with a hag and a mermaid screaming across a pond. It began earlier, in the Overgrown Manor campaign, after the planar fracture at Raventree Manor split local reality into overlapping states and the Feyward branch of Disaster Inc. was forced to navigate the Feywild-reflected version of the estate. Waluigi has written extensively elsewhere about the Oracle's synchronization ritual that caused the fracture, about Archie Miser's contribution to the ritual that made everything worse, and about how Waluigi raised concerns, was shushed, and will NEVER forgive the shushing.

Ferngrove Manor emerged during that broader campaign as one of the major satellite sites of the fractured region: a socially neutral house outwardly dedicated to hospitality and inwardly dedicated to deferring catastrophe until after tea. Saedia, the seneschal, presented the party with several household problems—the mermaid-hag dispute being one, the shambling plant monster eating staff being another, and the satyrs turning every room into an unlicensed pub being the third.

Waluigi took one look at the chore list and went to map the hedge maze. This was strategic prioritization. The maze contained dimensional anomalies that could connect to the castle transit network Waluigi has been documenting. The pond contained two screaming women. Waluigi chose science over sociology.

He arrived at the pond LATER, after the conflict had already escalated into fraud, confession, magical evidence recovery, attempted body transfer, and a dragon-related custody dispute. This is what happens when Waluigi leaves people unsupervised.

This record is therefore a synthesis of Waluigi's own observations, Hjumpik's account (enthusiastic but organizationally challenged), Toad Lee's notes (meticulous but emotionally restrained), and Waluigi's superior interpretive judgment. Where accounts conflict, Waluigi's version is correct. This is not arrogance. This is quality control.

## The Context: Why Ferngrove Manor Mattered

Ferngrove Manor sits in the Eastern Midlands near zones influenced by the Raventree line and along hidden fey pathways that do not appear on any sane map. Waluigi emphasizes the RAVENTREE proximity because this becomes important: the manor is approximately twelve kilometers from the Raventree Estate, which is the ancestral seat of a family whose name keeps appearing in intelligence reports connected to the Corvinarus bloodline, the Oracle's ritual, and the Grafting of 988 BF.

Twelve kilometers. In the Feywild, distance is negotiable, but even by Material Plane standards, this is CLOSE. Close enough that whatever infrastructure exists beneath Raventree might extend to Ferngrove. Close enough that fey roads connecting the two properties would be trivially short. Close enough that a Rakasha using a Midnight Portal at Ferngrove might be commuting to or from Raventree business.

Waluigi noted this proximity on his first day at the manor and filed it under 'coincidences that are not coincidences.' He has an entire filing cabinet for this category. It is the largest cabinet.

The manor itself functioned during the Feyward campaign as a social and logistical node where hostile entities, local nobility, stranded travelers, and semi-domesticated supernatural problems were all expected to coexist under one roof. Saedia attempted to maintain order by treating every crisis as a guest management issue. This included one screaming mermaid, one screaming hag, a grove beast called Shambly eating staff, and a population of satyrs who had overstayed their welcome by approximately three hundred percent.

Waluigi records this not to mock Saedia—though she deserves gentle mockery for her conflict-avoidance strategy of 'leaving two hostile supernatural entities to resolve their own conflict in an enclosed maze'—but to illustrate the atmosphere. Ferngrove did not solve problems. Ferngrove deferred them until they became folklore. And the moment a problem became folklore, it became Waluigi's job to document it.

The hedge maze outside the manor was not merely landscaping. It functioned as a semi-autonomous fey zone: paths shifted based on the traveler's emotional state, secluded pockets existed in spatial relationships that violated Euclidean geometry, and hidden clearings connected to older magical infrastructures. Waluigi spent his first three hours at Ferngrove measuring passage widths that changed depending on whether he was walking toward them or away from them. He recorded seventeen spatial inconsistencies, four temporal echoes (moments where the hedge seemed to remember a previous configuration and briefly revert to it), and one instance where a hedge wall was simply NOT THERE when he looked at it directly but was fully present in his peripheral vision.

The maze was alive. Not in the metaphorical sense. In the 'it was making decisions about who could go where' sense.

In other words, the pond was never 'just a pond.' It was a courtroom with lily pads, positioned in a maze that chose its own jury.

## What Waluigi Was Doing While Hjumpik Investigated the Pond

Waluigi wants this on the record because certain members of the party later implied he was 'not pulling his weight' during the investigation phase.

While Hjumpik and Toad Lee were at the pond listening to Herniva and Stuckina scream at each other, Waluigi was in the eastern section of the hedge maze conducting the following operations:

**Passage Mapping**: Waluigi identified and documented fourteen distinct pathways through the eastern maze, of which SIX did not exist on any map provided by Saedia's staff. Three of these pathways showed signs of recent use—freshly broken twigs, disturbed soil, and in one case, a footprint that did not match any species Waluigi could identify. The footprint had four toes, was approximately twenty centimeters long, and pressed deeper on the forward pad than the heel, indicating a creature that moved with predatory forward lean.

Waluigi did not follow this footprint. Waluigi is a genius, not a protagonist.

**Magical Frequency Analysis**: Using techniques borrowed from his castle transit network research, Waluigi detected three distinct magical frequencies emanating from below the maze. The first was consistent with standard fey road infrastructure—the ambient hum of maintained dimensional pathways. The second was something older, deeper, and rhythmic, like a heartbeat. The third was intermittent and directional, pulsing from the northeast toward the southwest at irregular intervals.

Waluigi later correlated the second frequency with the sleeping dragon's location. The heartbeat was LITERAL. There is a dragon sleeping beneath the hedge maze, and its heartbeat is detectable through magical frequency analysis. This is the kind of information that Waluigi considers critical and that everyone else apparently considers 'not urgent.'

The third frequency, the intermittent one, Waluigi has not yet identified. His working theory is that it relates to the Midnight Portal's activation cycle. If the portal pulses directionally, it may be receiving or transmitting data between the Ferngrove node and wherever it connects to.

**The Rakasha Observation**: Waluigi observed the Rakasha from behind a hedge approximately forty meters from the Midnight Portal's location. He did NOT approach. He did NOT attempt contact. He WATCHED, because watching is what intelligent people do when an unidentified member of a species connected to the most politically explosive bloodline secret in Mushroom Kingdom history appears in a maze near a dimensional portal.

The Rakasha moved with purpose. It was not exploring. It was NAVIGATING. It knew where the portal was. It was checking whether the portal was active, and once it confirmed activation, it entered immediately. The speed of its transition—no hesitation, no preparation ritual, no backward glance—suggests extensive prior experience with portal transit.

Waluigi's theory: this was not the Rakasha's first visit to Ferngrove Manor. The Midnight Portal is a regular transit point for Rakasha movement through the Midlands. They have been using fey infrastructure to travel unseen, possibly for decades, possibly for centuries.

If the Rakasha are connected to Chief Thornpaw's line—and by extension to the half-Rakasha child born of Peach's secret marriage—then they have had a LOGISTICS NETWORK for moving through hostile territory without detection for the entire duration of the post-assassination crisis. The Regency has been hunting for the Child of the Rose for eighty-five years. The Rakasha have been traveling through fey portals right under their noses.

Waluigi finds this simultaneously alarming and deeply satisfying. He does not like the Regency.

## How the Conversation at the Pond Actually Started

Waluigi was not present for the opening of the pond confrontation, but he has reconstructed it from Hjumpik's account and Toad Lee's considerably more precise notes.

Hjumpik and Toad Lee arrived at the pond after following the sound of sustained verbal abuse through the maze. Toad Lee's notes record that they could hear the argument from approximately two hundred meters away, which means either the pond has unusual acoustic properties (possible, given the fey zone's spatial distortions) or both women were screaming at volumes that should have attracted predators.

The pond itself was a carefully constructed space: hidden, secluded, with controlled access and the feel of a private chamber rather than a public garden. Waluigi suspects it was originally designed as a meditation space or a scrying pool. The lily pads, the candle poles, the platforms on either side—this was architecture, not nature. Someone built this pond for a PURPOSE, and that purpose was almost certainly not 'hosting screaming matches between mermaids and hags.'

Hjumpik entered first, assessed the situation with the tactical eye of someone who has been in enough bar fights to recognize the pre-violence tension phase, and made the critical decision to LISTEN before acting. This is, in Waluigi's professional opinion, the single most important thing Hjumpik did during the entire Ferngrove incident. Most people, confronted with two supernatural women accusing each other of crimes, would have either picked a side immediately or left. Hjumpik listened.

Stuckina's opening—'Just because I have a hideous face doesn't mean I'm a liar!'—told Waluigi everything he needed to know about the power dynamic even though he wasn't there to hear it. That sentence is the voice of someone who has been dismissed SO MANY TIMES on the basis of her appearance that she leads with a preemptive defense. She doesn't say 'I'm telling the truth.' She says 'my face doesn't make me wrong.' She has internalized the knowledge that her credibility is evaluated through her appearance, and she is trying to separate the two before anyone else can conflate them.

Herniva's response was, by contrast, the voice of someone who has NEVER had her credibility questioned. 'What would I want some stupid salty orb for?' is not a denial. It is a dismissal. It says: why would someone like ME bother with something belonging to someone like THAT? The question is rhetorical. The answer is assumed. Beautiful people don't steal from ugly people because beautiful people don't need to.

This is a lie so confident it forgets to be subtle.

## The Battle at the Grove: What Actually Happened

Waluigi was present for the grove confrontation with Ol' Shambly, and he has OPINIONS about how it was handled.

The party encountered the creature in a clearing where it had taken up residence near a root system that connected to the manor's deeper infrastructure. Shambly—also called Ol' Burley by the staff who had survived working near it—was a shambling mound of plant matter that had been tolerated as a 'beloved pet' and 'waste disposal system' until it started treating staff as waste.

Waluigi had seen Shambly before during the broader Overgrown Manor campaign. He knew its behavioral patterns: green when calm, dark purple when aggressive, and ALWAYS dangerous regardless of color because it was a sentient plant mass with the dietary preferences of a wood chipper.

The fight started when the party rounded a corner and found the Rakasha—not the Midnight Portal one, a different entity, Rakasha Azure—beneath Shambly's mass. The creature had apparently attacked Azure while the party was at the pond.

Toad Lee rushed in. This was brave. This was also exactly the kind of direct engagement that Waluigi has repeatedly argued against in tactical briefings that no one attends.

Stuckina was present—she had been following the party at a distance—and was knocked flying by one of Shambly's thrashing limbs. She hit the ground unconscious. Waluigi's steel defender barked—a sharp, mechanical sound that Waluigi had calibrated specifically for situations involving hostile biological entities.

Toad Lee, watching Shambly assault Azure and Stuckina, said something that Waluigi found uncharacteristically emotional: 'That thing's killing innocent people. He is losing patience.'

Toad Lee does not often express emotional urgency. When he does, it means the situation has exceeded his considerable threshold for tolerance. Waluigi took note.

Hjumpik's contribution was characteristically direct and effective. He leaped onto the creature's floral pedestal—the elevated mass at its center that functioned as both sensory hub and structural anchor—and struck what Waluigi can only describe as a weak point. The strike caused the creature to go limp, collapsing like a puppet with its strings cut.

Waluigi then proclaimed himself the winner of the fight.

He is aware that his direct combat contribution was limited. He provided tactical analysis, steel defender support, and the final authoritative declaration of victory. These are LEADERSHIP functions. Leaders do not need to hit things personally. Leaders need to be right about who won.

Waluigi was right. The fight was won. QED.

Hjumpik's first action after the creature fell was to check on Stuckina. He administered a healing potion—notably choosing a genuine, effective potion over a spoiled one he had in his inventory. This detail matters because it reveals Hjumpik's instinctive priorities: when someone is hurt, help them. Even if the someone is a hag. Even if helping them complicates the situation. Even if the politically convenient thing would be to let her remain unconscious while the adults sorted things out.

Hjumpik helped. Waluigi noted this and filed it under 'reasons Hjumpik is occasionally admirable despite his organizational deficiencies.'

## Waluigi's Conversation with Rakasha Azure: The Rest Period

After the grove fight, Hjumpik and Toad Lee continued their investigation while Waluigi and Rakasha Azure remained in the grove to rest and, in Waluigi's case, to think.

The rest period lasted approximately two hours. During this time, Waluigi and Azure had a conversation that Waluigi considers one of the more productive intelligence exchanges of the Feyward campaign.

Azure is difficult to evaluate. She is a Rakasha—which connects her, at least culturally, to Chief Thornpaw's people and by extension to the bloodline crisis at the heart of the assassination conspiracy. She appeared during the Overgrown Manor campaign under circumstances that suggested she was monitoring the party rather than coincidentally encountering them. She has been alternately helpful, evasive, flirtatious (primarily toward Hjumpik), and cryptic in ways that Waluigi recognizes as DELIBERATE information rationing.

She is not an ally. She is not an enemy. She is an asset with her own agenda, and Waluigi respects this because it is exactly what Waluigi would be in her position.

During the rest period, Waluigi shared his theory about the fey road infrastructure underlying the hedge maze. Azure listened without interrupting, which Waluigi appreciated, and then offered a comment that Waluigi has been turning over in his mind since:

'The roads are older than the courts. The courts are older than the kingdoms. The kingdoms are older than the calendars that count their years. You are asking good questions. But you are asking them as if the answers will fit inside the framework you already have.'

Waluigi asked her what she meant.

Azure smiled. 'Your calendar starts at a convenient number. Have you ever asked why?'

She did not elaborate. She closed her eyes and appeared to sleep.

Waluigi has not stopped thinking about this. The BF calendar—Before Foundation, the standard chronological system used across the Doughnut World—begins at a specific point. Year 1 BF. The founding of something. But Azure's implication is that the calendar's starting point is not the REAL beginning. It is a SELECTED beginning. A convenient number.

If the fey roads predate the courts, and the courts predate the kingdoms, and the kingdoms predate the calendars, then the entire historical framework Waluigi has been using to organize his intelligence is built on a foundation that someone CHOSE rather than discovered.

Who chose it? Why? What existed before year 1?

Azure knows. Azure is not telling.

This is extremely annoying.

## Waluigi Nearly Gets Scammed: The Treasure Offer

Waluigi must, in the interest of historical honesty, document his own near-failure.

While Hjumpik was negotiating Stuckina's release from Chirneros, Herniva approached Waluigi in the grove with an offer.

There was treasure, she said. Underground. Beneath the grove, in passages accessible through the hedge maze. Old treasure. Fey treasure. The kind of treasure that would make a man's reputation.

Waluigi was interested.

Waluigi is not proud of this. He KNOWS better. He has documented dozens of cases where promises of hidden wealth were used to lure victims into traps, exploitation, or worse. He has written EXTENSIVELY about how the powerful use promises of reward to manipulate the ambitious.

And then a pretty mermaid told him there was treasure underground and his first thought was 'how much?'

Azure, still resting nearby, opened one eye and said: 'Bad idea.'

Waluigi ignored Azure.

Azure said it again. 'Bad. Idea.'

Waluigi was approximately thirty seconds from following Herniva into whatever underground passage she was offering—thirty seconds from walking into a trap set by a woman he ALREADY KNEW was a thief, a liar, and a curser of innocent Toads—when Hjumpik returned from his Chirneros negotiation and shouted 'STOP!'

Waluigi stopped.

In retrospect, Waluigi understands that Herniva had identified his vulnerability—not greed exactly, but the particular form of ambition that makes Waluigi want to FIND things before anyone else does. She was not offering gold. She was offering DISCOVERY. The chance to be the first to map an unknown passage, to add to his intelligence files, to know something nobody else knew.

That is Waluigi's weakness. Not treasure. Information. And Herniva, who had spent years studying how to identify and exploit people's specific vulnerabilities, had read him correctly in under five minutes.

Hjumpik, who is approximately as subtle as a thrown brick, saved Waluigi from his own curiosity by simply yelling at him.

Waluigi is grateful. Waluigi will never say this out loud. Waluigi is saying it here, in an encyclopedia that Hjumpik will probably never read, because historical honesty demands it and because Waluigi can always delete this paragraph later.

## The Confrontation: Herniva's True Motive

After Hjumpik intervened and the treasure offer collapsed, the final confrontation with Herniva occurred.

Hjumpik asked the question that mattered: 'Why do you want to turn people into hags?'

Herniva's answer was delivered with a smile that Waluigi recognized immediately. It was the smile of someone who has stopped pretending and finds the truth more entertaining than the performance.

'So I can be the most pretty in the world. Everyone else will be ugly.'

Waluigi has spent considerable time analyzing this statement because it contains a logic that extends far beyond one vain mermaid.

Herniva does not want to be beautiful. Beauty is passive. Beauty is a state you maintain. Herniva wants to be THE MOST beautiful. Superlative beauty. Beauty defined not by its own qualities but by the ABSENCE of competition. She does not want to shine. She wants to be the only light in a room she has personally darkened.

This is not aesthetic preference. This is power architecture. Herniva is building a world in which her position is unassailable because she has systematically eliminated everyone who might challenge it.

Waluigi has seen this logic before:

- The Regency did not merely seize power after Peach's assassination. They spent eighty-five years eliminating everyone who might present an alternative.
- The Mages' Guild did not merely suppress the memory of the Shroob Incursion. They erased the TOOLS by which anyone might recover the memory independently.
- The Iron Legion does not merely conquer territory. They process the population to ensure no future resistance is structurally possible.

Herniva cursing Stuckina and stealing her scrying orb is the same logic applied at individual scale. Harm the vulnerable. Remove their means of recourse. Maintain social standing through the manufactured helplessness of others.

The pattern is fractal. It repeats at every scale. From a mermaid in a pond to an empire spanning the Midlands.

Waluigi finds this the most important insight of the entire Ferngrove incident, and he discovered it while being rescued from a treasure scam by a dwarf with a cowbell.

Historical irony is Waluigi's least favorite form of irony.

WAH. Waluigi is rewriting this AGAIN because the original verbal summary offended his sense of chronology, aesthetics, and basic investigative dignity.

The encounter at Ferngrove Manor did not begin with a hag and a mermaid screaming across a pond. It began earlier, in the Overgrown Manor campaign, after the planar fracture at Raventree Manor split local reality into overlapping states and the Feyward branch of Disaster Inc. was forced to navigate the Feywild-reflected version of the estate. Ferngrove Manor emerged during that broader campaign as one of the major satellite sites of the fractured region: a socially neutral house outwardly dedicated to hospitality and inwardly dedicated to deferring catastrophe until after tea.

Saedia, seneschal of the manor, presented the party with several household problems. One of them was the conflict between two missing guests: Herniva, a mermaid, and Stuckina, a hag. They had been in the maze for some time, shrieking at one another from opposite sides of a pond while everyone else in the manor quietly developed headaches.

Waluigi was not present for the earliest exchange at the pond. Waluigi was conducting legitimate dimensional reconnaissance in the hedge system and absolutely not hiding from social obligations. He arrived later, after the conflict had already escalated into fraud, confession, magical evidence recovery, attempted body transfer, and a dragon-related custody dispute.

This record is therefore a synthesis of Waluigi's own observations, Hjumpik's account, Toad Lee's notes, and Waluigi's superior interpretive judgment.

## The Context: Why Ferngrove Manor Mattered

Ferngrove Manor sits in the Eastern Midlands near zones influenced by the Raventree line and along hidden fey pathways that do not appear on any sane map. It functioned during the Feyward campaign as a social and logistical node where hostile entities, local nobility, stranded travelers, and semi-domesticated supernatural problems were all expected to coexist under one roof.

This was, of course, impossible.

Saedia attempted to maintain order by treating every crisis as a guest management issue. This included one screaming mermaid, one screaming hag, and a grove beast called Shambly eating staff. Waluigi records this not to mock Saedia—though mocking is deserved—but to illustrate the atmosphere in which the hag incident occurred. Ferngrove did not solve problems. Ferngrove deferred them until they became folklore.

The hedge maze outside the manor was not merely landscaping. It functioned as a semi-autonomous fey zone: paths shifted, secluded pockets existed in impossible spatial relationships, and hidden clearings connected to older magical infrastructures, including what the party would later identify as the Midnight Portal and the grove containing the sleeping dragon.

In other words, the pond was never 'just a pond.' It was a courtroom with lily pads.

## The Initial Complaint: Stuckina's Orb

When Hjumpik and Toad Lee located the two disputants, they found them seated on opposite platforms overlooking a small hidden pond. The water was green, murky, and threaded with lily pads. Candled poles rose from the pond's middle. Both women looked deeply irritated. Both had likely been insulting each other for hours.

Stuckina spoke first and immediately established the emotional register of the exchange:

'Just because I have a hideous face doesn't mean I'm a liar! Listen—she stole my orb. I KNOW she stole it.'

This is one of the clearest opening statements Waluigi has ever seen from a victim who already knows no one will believe her.

Hjumpik, to his credit, did not dismiss her. He asked what kind of orb it was.

Stuckina clarified that it was not some great artifact of sorcery but 'just a mundane orb from my childhood'—which made the intensity of her reaction seem disproportionate until later evidence revealed the truth. It was not merely sentimental. She intended to use the orb for scrying. It was, functionally, the one object she still possessed that might have told her who had ruined her life.

Her offered payment escalated quickly—gold, silver, anything, and then murder. Specifically: cut off Herniva's tail and kill the siren.

Waluigi does not endorse this solution. Waluigi understands the impulse.

## Herniva's Denial

Herniva's response was elegant, contemptuous, and immediately suspicious.

She dismissed Stuckina's claim, mocked both the orb and its owner, and argued that if Stuckina had once possessed such an item she had probably dropped it in the maze. She framed Stuckina's accusation as jealousy—claiming the hag resented her beauty and station.

This would have been ordinary cruelty if it had not later proven to be active concealment.

When pressed, Herniva consented to a search with performative confidence. This was a mistake, but only because she misjudged Hjumpik's persistence and the properties of the object he was carrying.

The search of her satchels produced only one suspicious object: a carved quartz skull roughly orb-sized. It was not pearl. It was not round. It was, Herniva argued, obviously not the item in question.

At this stage, with no visible orb, no hard proof, and only Stuckina's certainty against Herniva's poise, the confrontation might have ended there.

It did not.

Because Hjumpik had the Cowbell of Raventree.

## The Cowbell and the Skull

Waluigi would like the record to show that he has, in the past, questioned the utility of Hjumpik carrying a cowbell into delicate investigative situations.

Waluigi was wrong.

Hjumpik requested to inspect the quartz skull one final time. Herniva, now visibly calmer and apparently certain she had passed the search, handed it over with a smile. Hjumpik rang the Cowbell of Raventree.

The object glowed. Its shape softened. The skull rounded and reformed into a smooth pearl orb.

At that moment, the entire dispute changed character.

This was no longer a matter of accusation. It was a matter of proof.

Herniva immediately tried to reclaim the object. Hjumpik refused and stated, quite sensibly, that he intended to show it to Stuckina.

Toad Lee observed that he had no opinion on the social implications of this exchange. Waluigi respects this form of strategic neutrality, though only in others.

What mattered is that the bell revealed the disguised object for what it truly was. This establishes two critical facts:

1. The Cowbell of Raventree can break or expose active concealment magic.
2. Herniva had not merely stolen the orb. She had altered its appearance and kept it on her person.

The theft was deliberate. The disguise was deliberate. The concealment was sustained. This was not a misunderstanding. It was evidence suppression.

## Herniva's Confession

Once the skull was revealed as the orb, Herniva's position collapsed. She confessed.

What she confessed to matters far more than the theft.

When younger, she had treated cruelty as recreation. She spoke casually of mermaid customs—luring ships to rocks, tormenting sailors, enjoying tricks played on the vulnerable because beauty and cleverness justified the sport. One day, in a river, she saw a Toad gathering plants. She intended only to frighten her—pull her into the water, laugh, and leave.

Instead the Toad struck her accidentally while falling. Herniva became angry. She cursed her on impulse.

The cursed Toad was Stuckina Boggs.

The same Stuckina Boggs who had once operated Aul Nan's Apothecary in Ferncombe. The same Stuckina who had grown up near the Raventree Estate. The same Stuckina who had spent years trapped in a body and social role she had not chosen.

Herniva did not stop there. She left Stuckina in a cave. Later, once she understood that the orb could be used for scrying, she stole it to prevent Stuckina from learning the truth.

Waluigi's interpretation is blunt: Herniva transformed a Toad woman into a hag through impulsive cruelty, abandoned her, then spent years ensuring the victim could not identify her attacker.

This is not a personality conflict. It is a sustained crime.

## Why the Orb Mattered

The orb was not merely a sentimental keepsake from childhood. It was Stuckina's intended means of scrying the source of her curse.

This detail matters for three reasons.

First, it proves Stuckina had not lost interest in her own history. She had been actively trying to reclaim the truth of what happened to her.

Second, it confirms that Herniva understood the orb's function and specifically targeted it. She was not stealing at random. She was stealing the means of accountability.

Third, it demonstrates a broader pattern Waluigi has seen elsewhere in the Mushroom Kingdom and beyond: the powerful not only harm the vulnerable, they remove the tools by which the vulnerable could prove they were harmed.

Herniva's conduct is structurally similar to Regency archival suppression, Mages' Guild memory intervention, and the political disappearance of evidence in dynastic crimes. The scale is smaller. The logic is the same.

## Toad Lee's Lead

During the confession, Hjumpik asked Herniva for more detail about the victim she had cursed.

Herniva described a Toad with pink dots and pigtails. Toad Lee immediately noted the description, though he clarified that he was looking for missing Toads and did not believe it matched the one he had been pursuing.

This is still significant.

The curse of Stuckina Boggs places another displaced Toad on Toad Lee's growing map of vanished, transformed, erased, or socially displaced Toad persons in the Midlands. Even if Stuckina was not one of his original targets, her case reinforces the pattern.

Toad disappearances are not all abductions. Some are curses. Some are social erasures. Some are transformations severe enough that the victim ceases to be recognized as Toad at all.

Waluigi considers this a major investigative development hiding inside what most people would dismiss as a local feud.

## The Rakasha and the Midnight Portal

Before the dispute at the pond, the party had already observed a Rakasha searching for what seemed to be a hidden route through the manor grounds. The Rakasha repeatedly tried to draw Hjumpik into a naming exchange, identified itself only as 'Rakasha,' then located the Midnight Portal, entered it, and vanished. The portal immediately deactivated.

Waluigi considers this one of the most important background details of the entire incident.

The Rakasha's presence at Ferngrove Manor links the site to the broader Rakasha movement in the region, and by extension to the old Thornpaw line, to the hidden marriage of Princess Peach, and to the surviving blood questions at the center of Mushroom Kingdom legitimacy. The portal was active before the pond conflict and inactive after the Rakasha passed through it. This suggests Ferngrove Manor's hidden pathways are still in live use by actors with access to older magical infrastructures.

Waluigi has a working theory that the Midnight Portal is part of the same deep transit ecology that underlies the fey roads, the Raventree anomalies, and portions of Peach's Castle's dimensional behavior. He is not yet prepared to claim this as fact. He is absolutely prepared to say it is BAD.

## The Grove, Shambly, and Waluigi's Presence

Waluigi enters the incident directly during the grove confrontation.

By this stage, the party had moved from argument resolution to active field danger. They encountered Ol' Shambly, a manor mascot and grove beast whose preferred diet included staff. Toad Lee engaged. Stuckina was knocked unconscious in the confusion. Waluigi and Rakasha Azure were nearby when Hjumpik identified a weakness and disabled the creature.

Waluigi would like the record to note that he contributed to the fight and therefore was entitled to proclaim himself the winner afterward.

He then remained in the grove with Rakasha Azure while Hjumpik and Toad Lee continued sorting out the hag-mermaid affair. During this period Waluigi explained why he was at Ferngrove at all: he had been tracking anomalies in the local transit ecology and suspected the manor sat on or near older fey road infrastructure. He also noted, correctly, that too many people in this region were pretending not to notice impossible geography.

Waluigi was in the middle of articulating a very good theory when Herniva approached him with an offer of hidden underground treasure.

Waluigi was interested. Briefly.

Azure told him it was a bad idea.

Azure was right.

## Chirneros and the Sleeping Dragon

The incident escalated dramatically when Herniva attempted to have Stuckina removed and delivered to Chirneros, a stag-born fey lord deep in the manor grounds.

Chirneros was preparing to wake a sleeping dragon by using the life force of 'a hag.'

Hjumpik objected on the grounds that Stuckina was not naturally a hag at all, but a cursed Toad. This prompted one of the most important revelations in the entire Ferngrove sequence.

Chirneros explained that the dragon had been put to sleep in 988 BF through a blood ritual called the Grafting. According to him, a previous heir cut their palm over a dragon egg, the Legion was present, and the hatched dragon is the same adult creature now sleeping beneath the grove.

This matters enormously.

The Grafting links the manor incident directly to older bloodline engineering and dragon-binding practices associated with noble succession and Legion oversight. It implies:

- a ritual continuity from 988 BF into the present,
- active or residual draconic power in a local heir line,
- and prior Iron Legion knowledge of blood pact techniques involving living apex entities.

Waluigi does not know which heir line was involved. He very much wants to.

## Stuckina's Testimony

After being revived, Stuckina provided crucial personal history.

She was once Stuckina Boggs, proprietor of Aul Nan's Apothecary in Ferncombe. She inherited the shop after her mother's death. She was gathering materials along the river when Herniva attacked and cursed her.

This confirms Stuckina as:

- local,
- socially rooted,
- economically independent before the curse,
- and connected to a known settlement near the Raventree sphere.

She had retained enough magic to disguise herself temporarily as a human woman—though Hjumpik's attempts to improve the disguise made it worse, which Waluigi finds completely believable.

Most importantly, when shown the recovered orb, she identified its intended use: scrying the source of her curse.

The orb was her path back to truth.

Herniva stole that path.

## Herniva's Final Position

When confronted again later, Herniva did not deny her broader intentions.

Asked why she wanted to turn others into hags, she answered with chilling simplicity:

'So I can be the most pretty in the world. Everyone else will be ugly.'

That is not metaphor. That is motive.

Herniva's worldview is aesthetic supremacy through the manufactured degradation of others. She does not want beauty. She wants COMPARATIVE beauty. She wants a world where her appearance wins by default because everyone else has been ruined.

This makes her one of the purest expressions of vanity as political violence that Waluigi has yet documented.

She also attempted to preserve the deal structure by insisting the agreement with the party was still valid if they fulfilled their side. Waluigi's reading is that she understood perfectly well how to exploit ambiguity in promises while preserving future leverage.

In other words, she would make an excellent courtier in the Regency.

## Outcome and Unresolved Questions

The immediate outcome was partial.

The truth was established. The orb was recovered. Herniva confessed. Stuckina's false social identity was pierced and her original name restored to the historical record. Chirneros's attempt to use her as sacrificial fuel was interrupted.

But much remains unresolved.

Stuckina is still cursed.

The dragon is still sleeping.

Chirneros still wants it awakened.

The Grafting remains only partially understood.

The Rakasha escaped through the Midnight Portal.

Saedia still needs to be confronted with the uncursing question.

And Herniva is still in circulation, smiling at people.

Waluigi hates the smiling part the most.

## Waluigi's Assessment

The Hag of Ferngrove Manor is not a side story. It is a structural clue.

A Toad was erased through a curse and had the evidence hidden from her. A fey lord attempted to convert the cursed victim into ritual fuel. A dragon sleeps under old blood law. A Rakasha uses a hidden portal nearby. A seneschal treats all of this as guest management. And a mermaid with the moral depth of a teaspoon tries to sell everyone else ugliness so she can feel special.

This is the Feywild version of the larger world crisis in miniature.

The vulnerable are transformed. The truth is disguised. The evidence is stolen. The powerful insist on etiquette while preparing ritual violence. And underneath it all, old infrastructures continue humming—portals, blood pacts, sleeping monsters, inherited obligations.

Waluigi was there long enough to recognize the pattern and smart enough to leave before accepting any treasure from anyone with fins.

This alone marks the incident as a qualified success.

WAH.
