name: The Shadow Estate Campaign
title: Vampires, Vats, and the Heir Who Died Laughing
date: 21st Highsun through 4th Harvestide, 1040 BF (Shadowfell slowness applied)
location: The Shadow Estate, Shadowfell
type: Dimensional Campaign / Survival / Assassination / Infiltration
status: Ongoing — Shadow Anchor shattered, Vivian Corvinarus killed, Parallel Dan identified, Mages Guild oversight established
summary: Waluigi is documenting the Shadow Estate Campaign as a masterclass in gothic incompetence and aristocratic cruelty. The Shadowfell fragment of Disaster Inc. began with Archie Miser losing his fire magic and Bowser trying to eat raw vampire meat, and it has since spiraled into a multi-layered nightmare involving a silver bullet, a cross-dressing heir who was ultimately stabbed to death while laughing, and a parallel version of Dan who silenced the original. Waluigi has learned that in the Shadowfell, every dinner party is a death sentence, every mirror is a one-way surveillance tool, and every 'friendship ring' is actually a tracking device that leaks entropy. Between Green T's sniper skills, Remi's transformation into a disco ball, and the discovery of necromantic abomination vats, Waluigi is increasingly convinced that the Shadowfell is the dimension where logic goes to die and be resurrected as a singing ghoul. Waluigi frankly finds it insulting that they get to have a gothic horror adventure while Waluigi is forced to weave daisy chains for condescending tree-spirits. If Waluigi were in the Shadowfell, he would have bought the manor, evicted the vampires, and turned the Shadow Anchor into a tennis trophy. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the Shadow Estate Campaign from reconstructed reports, stolen diaries, secondhand accounts, and the haunted expression on Markop's face every time someone mentions dinner parties. Unlike the Feywild, which buried the party in flowers and etiquette, the Shadowfell buried them in greyscale dread, administrative murder, and the kind of gothic hospitality where the appetizer is raw meat and the dessert is a vote on who dies. The following is the definitive account of the Shadow Estate stay, organized chronologically to the extent that chronology functions in a dimension where time flows like cold syrup through a broken hourglass.

## The Cold Awakening (21st Highsun, 02:00)

The Shadowfell campaign began in the worst possible way: Archie Miser woke up on a cold marble floor without his fire.

Waluigi wants readers to understand what that means. Archie without fire is like Waluigi without his hat—technically alive but spiritually incomplete. The dimension's entropy was so high and its energy so low that Archie's fingers produced only cold grey smoke when he snapped them. He tried once, twice, three times, each attempt more desperate than the last. Nothing. A tiny spark appeared on the second attempt and instantly died, swallowed by the ambient suppression like a match dropped in a river.

Waluigi finds Archie’s panic pathetic. When Waluigi loses a tennis match, does he cry? No, he breaks his racket over the umpire's knee! Archie without fire is just a man with a bad hat. WAH!

Bowser groaned beside him and said 'get off me you plumbing accident,' which Archie took personally since he is not Mario and has never been Mario and resents the comparison. Bowser stood up, looked around at the colorless world—black, white, and shades of grey with no warmth anywhere—and asked where they were. When Archie explained that physics were wrong here, that entropy was high and energy was low, Bowser punched a wall. It cracked, but the sound was dampened, as though the dimension itself was absorbing noise the way it absorbed color and heat and hope.

The hallway they walked through was pristine, unlike the ruined manor they had left behind. Dark velvet wallpaper dressed the walls, and sconces held cold white flames that offered no heat. There was no dust. There was no life. The windows showed a sky of swirling bruised purple clouds and a landscape of dead petrified trees stretching to a horizon that looked like it had given up on the concept of distance.

A toad in a tuxedo stepped out of the shadows. His skin was pale grey and his eyes were red like embers that had forgotten they were supposed to be warm. He informed them that Master Cornelius was expecting them for the main course. Bowser roared about being King Bowser, but the butler did not flinch, merely noting that the master did not like loud noises. Archie whispered for Bowser to play along because he had no magic. Bowser grumbled but agreed, adding that if the food was bad he would burn the place down. Archie reminded him that neither of them could burn anything. Bowser said he had fists.

Waluigi respects this exchange because it established the dynamic that would carry the entire Shadowfell campaign: Archie thinking, Bowser punching, and the dimension ignoring both of them. Though Waluigi must ask—why didn't Bowser just eat the butler? If you're going to be a monstrous turtle king, act like it!

## The Dinner of the Onyx Hand (22nd Highsun, Evening)

The dining hall was a mirror of the Feywild version but twisted into gothic opulence that made Waluigi's skin crawl just hearing about it. The table was long polished ebony. High-backed chairs sat like thrones around it. The chandeliers dripped with wax that looked suspiciously like coagulated blood, because in the Shadowfell even the interior decoration wants you to know that something is wrong.

Seated around the table were figures of elegance and dread—vampires, shades, and pale nobles of the Onyx Hand. At the head sat Orangus Cornelius, a toad but tall, with sharp fangs and skin that would have been orange if color existed in this dimension. He held a goblet of thick red liquid and greeted them with the words 'welcome guests, you are late,' which is the most vampire thing anyone has ever said and also the most annoying because Archie and Bowser did not ask to be here and were not given a schedule.

Bowser sat down at the opposite end of the table and said 'nice place, a bit gloomy.' Cornelius smiled and said they preferred the term 'atmospheric.' Waluigi suspects this is the Shadowfell's official tourism slogan.

Archie looked to the side and saw a small table—the kids' table. Green T was there, wearing a bib, looking terrified. But he made eye contact with Archie and tapped his spoon against the table in what could have been morse code but was probably just nerves. Then Green T moved his hand under the table and flashed something: a flintlock pistol. Where he got it remains one of the campaign's minor mysteries. Waluigi's theory is that Green T has been smuggling weapons in places nobody checks since the Syndicate days, and anyone who seats a former crime lord at the children's table deserves what happens next.

Waluigi has attended many evil dinner parties, and there is a strict etiquette to these things. You do not bring a flintlock to the appetizer course unless it is a formal duel! But Waluigi must admit, shooting the host before dessert is a power move. Waluigi is taking notes.

Servants brought out plates of raw, dripping meat. Bowser ate his in one bite and called it a good steak, a bit rare. Archie stared at his plate and was told by Cornelius that it was rude to refuse a host. Then the real conversation began.

Cornelius stood and accused Archie of burning his greenhouse in the Material Plane. He had built that glass to hold the sunlight, he explained, because they did not get sun in the Shadowfell. Archie sweated and claimed it was an accident involving rust monsters. Cornelius walked closer and said Archie owed him a debt. Bowser stood up and said Archie owed nothing to a frog-face, at which point Cornelius threatened to turn Bowser's shell into a soup bowl, the vampires hissed, and weapons were drawn throughout the room.

Archie tried to negotiate. Cornelius laughed and asked what Archie could possibly offer when his magic was gone and his friends were scattered. Then Green T stood up from the children's table and said 'he has me, and I have the key to the anchor.' Cornelius's face dropped. He ordered Green T seized.

## The Standoff and the Shattering of the Shadow Anchor (23rd Highsun)

Green T kicked the kids' table over and shouted for Archie to run. Bowser flipped the main table, sending plates and goblets and raw meat flying everywhere. Vampires screamed. Archie grabbed a silver candlestick because silver burns vampires and because Archie's improvisation instincts are genuinely impressive when he cannot rely on fire. He swung the candlestick into a vampire and it connected, the creature hissing and burning from the contact.

Bowser tackled Cornelius directly. They crashed through a window into the courtyard below, which is the most Bowser solution to any indoor problem: remove the indoors. Green T fired his pistol—the chandelier crashed down—and Archie yelled asking where the exit was. Green T yelled back that they needed to break the mirror in the attic, but Bowser was already outside wrestling Cornelius in his true form: a giant bat monster.

Archie jumped out the window after Bowser. Gravity was lower in the Shadowfell, so he floated down like a dandelion and landed on Bowser's shell. Below them, Bowser was biting the bat monster's wing with the confidence of someone whose immune system has never heard the word 'impossible.' Archie tried to spark any spell at all—not fire, just light, just a spark—and produced nothing but a fizzle.

Bowser threw Cornelius into a winged statue in the courtyard. The statue broke. It was hollow. Inside was a glowing purple crystal: the Shadow Anchor. This was the device maintaining the Shadowfell's planar suppression, the thing keeping fire dead and color absent and the whole dimension locked in its entropic state. Archie realized what it was instantly and screamed for Bowser to smash it.

Bowser wound up a punch. Cornelius recovered and lunged to protect the crystal. Time slowed. Green T appeared at the broken window above, took aim with his flintlock, and fired a single silver bullet.

The bullet hit the crystal.

The Anchor shattered.

Reality cracked along seams that had been invisible until that moment. Color bled back into the world—reds, oranges, yellows returning violently, making the gothic architecture look simultaneously magnificent and absurd. Fire returned to Archie's hands. He felt the heat and smiled and said 'ignite,' which is the closest thing Archie has to a prayer.

Waluigi wants the record to show that the Shadow Anchor was destroyed by a former tea merchant sitting at the children's table with a stolen flintlock. Green T's trajectory from crime lord to mirror-dimension survivor to vampire dinner party sniper remains one of the most remarkable character arcs in the entire campaign. Waluigi demands an investigation into Green T's background. You do not go from selling herbal tea to no-scoping a dimensional anchor while dodging vampire bats unless you have a history of extreme violence. Waluigi suspects tax evasion. WAH.

## The Ballroom of Boneless Dancers (24th Highsun)

While the anchor battle raged in the courtyard, Markop's group was fighting for their lives inside the manor's ballroom. Toadburt was being pulled apart by undead dancers—boneless ghouls contorting their bodies in unpredictable ways, twisting and writhing to an endless song that seemed to come from no particular direction. The dance hall was thick with the smell of old sweat, and the floor was smeared with old blood and spilled drink. Broken crossbow bolts were scattered everywhere, some still embedded in the wood.

Perrius Annmatar touched one of the dancers and burned its skin on contact. Markop used Divine Smite and tossed a crossbow to Bowser, who fired bolts into the dancers' shins with the accuracy of someone who treats ranged weapons as a minor inconvenience between punches. The dancers surrounded Markop and kicked his shins until he cried out in pain. One dancer seized Toadburt and dragged him away as he screamed and his ribs cracked under the pressure.

The Onyx Hand breached the ballroom doors. Bowser went flying from the impact. Markop swung his axe and dropped a dancer, then rushed to help Toadburt, only to be grappled himself by a torso-and-hands-only dancer that had lost its legs but not its enthusiasm for violence. Salam opened the opposite door to the ballroom, ignoring Markop's instructions entirely, and asked who he should whip. Eager ran past an Onyx guard, ducked beneath a headless dancer, and entered through the other side.

Bowser eventually used his restored fire breath to incinerate the zombies. The dancers collapsed, their bodies bleeding and deflating as the fire consumed them. Bowser punched one into the wall for good measure. A deal was struck with the Onyx Hand: they would help the injured Toadburt in exchange for the party eliminating the remaining headless dancers. Toadburt's ribs were cracked, and he would later be taken to the Archivist for healing in exchange for indentured library work.

Waluigi is an expert dancer, and he is deeply offended by the very concept of boneless zombies ruining a perfectly good ballroom. Where is the posture? Where is the panache? If Waluigi were there, he would have challenged the torso-monster to a dance-off and won through sheer leg-extension. Markop using a battleaxe is just poor choreography. WAH.

## Archie and Green T's Escape Through the Manor

After the anchor shattered, Archie and Green T found themselves trapped inside the manor proper, separated from Bowser and surrounded by vampires who were adjusting to the sudden return of color and heat. Green T commented that Archie's friends were probably dead by now, having been gone for two days. Archie insisted they would be fine.

They tried to leave but found the door locked. Footsteps approached. Green T ran. Archie ran behind him, opening doors at random: one led to a vampire cooking meat who said 'oh good, more meat for dinner'; another led to an operating room where a vampire was performing surgery on a human body with clinical precision. They got separated. Archie barricaded himself in a room with a coffin while something banged on the door.

Archie focused his partially restored energy and shattered the door, running out and shouting for Green T. He cast a disguise on himself—a vampire face over his own—and ran to a window where Green T was trapped, unable to jump out because the glass was jammed. A vampire was going through files nearby, and Archie, in his disguise, identified himself as 'Dracacide.' The vampire asked if he had seen a green being. Archie said nope. Green T sneaked out of his hiding spot under a bed, past the distracted vampire, and they moved through the manor together, passing through a barricaded room, a study Green T described as boring, and finally into the main reception area.

Waluigi thinks Archie’s disguise of 'Dracacide' is the stupidest fake name he has ever heard. Waluigi has used aliases like 'Waluigi' with a fake mustache over his real mustache, and it was infinitely more convincing!

Archie handed Green T a dagger for quieter combat. They exited the manor and spent two days walking to what turned out to be the crashed airship, now swarmed by troops broadcasting compliance announcements through loudspeakers: 'ATTENTION CITIZENS. THE ANOMALY IS CONTAINED. COMPLIANCE IS MANDATORY. REPORT ALL NON-HUMAN ACTIVITY. ORDER IS SAFETY.'

Archie disguised himself as a guard and infiltrated the crash site. He learned that the troops called themselves the Purple Legion and claimed to rule the 'Vamp Lands' from coast to coast. A guard gave him a map and Archie recognized it as the Midlands geography but rendered in purple. Dan's cage at the crash site was empty. A mysterious figure named Orvinder Danos appeared—a barrister with neat dark hair, a cane he did not need, and a commitment to truth that bordered on pathological.

Orvinder led Archie to a back room with a portal and introduced him to Usk, who was split between three manors and needed help reuniting. Archie declined to help immediately because he was focused on finding his friends. They returned to the crash site, where a guard named Vin joined Archie's improvised investigation team, and another vampire Archie nicknamed 'Blorb' pulled out a mushroom when asked if he had found a toad.

Archie wandered between the crash site, a tavern called the Shadowfell Inn, and eventually back to the manor over the course of days. Green T disappeared while Archie was distracted. Archie spent weeks alone—living in the forest, returning to the manor periodically to find it increasingly restored and hostile. A month passed. The manor flashed, the walls crumbled, and Archie was suddenly back in the Ruined Manor's mirror room with Usk, Orvinder, and Mages Guild agents waiting for him.

## The Mages Guild Drafts Archie

The Mages Guild agents surrounded Archie and informed him that his magic 'bled entropy' and that he was the reason the portal had unexpectedly opened. They revealed that Toadburt had been their sleeper agent, equipped with an Entropy Ring to tag Archie for capture. When the sleeper operation failed, Archie's own arrival accomplished what the agent could not.

The agents argued among themselves about whether the portal was their fault or Archie's fault. They revealed a 'Regulator Plane'—a fourth bridge plane designed to connect the Feyward, Shadeward, and Ruined manors. This bridge could be collapsed to sever the connections permanently, potentially destroying two-thirds of reality to stabilize the remainder.

Archie was told he now worked for the Mages Guild. His immense power came with immense responsibility and oversight. He had no choice. They introduced him to their newest team member: Luigi, who bumped into the door frame as he entered.

Waluigi loves bureaucracy when it is punishing people Waluigi dislikes. Putting Archie on a managerial leash is poetry. But introducing Luigi? WAH! The green menace ruins everything! Waluigi bets Luigi tripped over his own shoelaces while trying to look authoritative.

## Remi's Solo Investigation and the Disco Ball

Remi's thread through the Shadowfell is a study in resilience, bad judgment, and the discovery that glowing like a sun in a dimension of perpetual darkness makes you simultaneously the most visible and most useful person in any room.

After the dinner chaos, Remi was surrounded by guards and interrogated. She answered their questions with her characteristic directness: she did not know what the candy she gave the guard was called, she was not working for anyone, she was not aligned with any faction, and she was 'just along for the ride.' She was dismissed and walked the dining hall alone.

In the bathroom she found a spent casing on the ground with a giant 'W' logo on it—Green T's bullet from the flintlock. She called over a guard and showed them, noting that the trajectory did not match the shooting position. Something was not adding up. She met Kryn Cornelius, who introduced himself as heir to the throne of Autumnwood. She examined the casing in the Oracle's wound and confirmed it matched.

Remi went to Vivesna—who was ecstatic, practically vibrating with barely contained triumph. Remi noticed the wig and said 'oh my, your hair is fake.' Vivian, not yet unmasked, explained casually that he was waiting for both the Oracle and Orangus to die so he could become the new heir. He told Remi to leave and let nature take its course.

Kyrn gave Remi keys to the lord's chambers, where she explored extensively. The master bedroom was luxurious—red furnishings, silver vases filled with roses whose petals seemed made of clotted blood, a four-post bed with velvet curtains, and a commanding view of bleak dark lands. In the medicine cabinet she found vampiric healing supplies: Hemoglue of the Nightlord, Shadowveil Tincture, Stakeheart Salve, Leadfang Extractor, and Ebonblood Antidote. She took two.

Beneath the rug in the center of the room she discovered a broken teleportation circle etched in chalk and charcoal—irreparably damaged but with about a third still glowing faintly with ancient power. She rolled the carpet back up and left.

A guard later offered Remi a glowing vial as a remedy for the news that her friends were dead (a lie she accepted with disturbing calm). She chugged the vial. On the 1st of Harvestide, Remi began glowing with radiant light so bright it blinded everyone around her. 'I'm like a disco,' she observed.

Waluigi would like to point out the absolute idiocy of drinking a mysterious glowing vial in a dimension actively trying to kill you. Becoming a disco ball is stylish, yes. Waluigi respects the aesthetic. But as a tactical choice? It is like painting a bullseye on your forehead and lighting it on fire.

Remi encountered Toadburt in the library, now missing his Entropy Ring and working for the Archivist. She helped imps organize fallen bookshelves, found an expired coupon with Wario's phone number in her pocket, and eventually reunited with Markop and Bowser in the lobby. Markop squinted at her glowing form and asked why she was a disco ball. She shrugged.

## The Purple Toad's Deal and Remi's Purple Eyes

The purple toad who had given Remi the glowing potion reappeared and offered her a deal: he would bring her home in exchange for her 'eyes'—not physically, but her mental perception, her ability to see clearly through deception and manipulation. Remi agreed. Her glow faded. Her eyes turned purple. The deal was sealed.

Waluigi is surrounded by fools. 'I will trade my perception for a ride home!' Do you know what happens when you trade your perception, Remi? You start trusting people in purple! And nobody in purple should be trusted, except Waluigi. WAH!

The purple toad laughed and was immediately grabbed by Shadowfell guards for performing unauthorized magic within the estate. The guards then brought Remi to the infirmary, where attendants proposed placing an entropy-blocking ring on her to prevent outside magical interference during their examination. The party recognized this for what it was: another obedience collar, the same kind the Iron Legion had used on Toadburt. A standoff ensued with guards positioned at every corner of the room.

Marcus Ashford—Orangus Cornelius's military consultant—entered and offered Remi a different remedy, which turned both her eyes blue. Markop noticed they were one tint lighter than before and that black smoke was leaking from the gash where an Onyx Hand knight had 'accidentally' cut her eye earlier. Remi claimed the smoke was part of the healing process. Markop was unconvinced but lacked evidence to push further.

## Vivian's Corridor Ambush and Death

Vivian Corvinarus had been operating inside the manor for weeks under the thrall disguise 'Vivesna.' The name shuffled between Vivesna, Vinvessa, and Vivian depending on which persona was active—a sophisticated triple-identity system that suggested years of practice at being multiple people simultaneously.

Dan responded that they had kept him fed. Markop said that was what they did to prisoners. Dan ran away crying, bumping into Bowser, who took two items from him. Bowser then said he wished 'Toadstool was here' and revealed his full royal name as Sir Koopa Frederickson the Fifteenth.

Remi chased a butterfly to the river. Eager chased after her. Salam began woodcarving. Markop said they needed to stop getting off topic.

## Lyranth the Sculptor and the Bidding War

Remi entered the Sculptor's workshop—a chaos of hammers, chisels, and stone dust where Lyranth the Medusa worked surrounded by half-finished marble figures of astounding artistry. Lyranth had covered her marble-veined skin in vibrant paint to avoid being mistaken for her own creations. Her crown of snakes swayed independently. She looked at Remi, said 'smile,' and turned her to stone.

Petrified Remi was displayed at an art exhibit and put up for a bidding war. Mystic Morel won the bid for 12,000 gold. A brawl erupted: Markop shattered a window, Wario shoulder-bashed Markop from behind, a Mages Guild agent stabbed Wario, Bowser pulled out a device to call his son for support, Markop summoned a moonbeam, and Salam started picking flowers during the chaos because apparently some people cope with combat through botany.

Remi was freed from stone form and jumped into Dan's arms. Morel followed them, insisting he had to keep his 'end of the deal.' The toads told him to leave. Remi said he could be their friend. Morel offered tea, then incense, each rejected by the increasingly paranoid toad contingent. Remi asked how much she had been bid for. Twelve thousand gold. Waluigi finds it revealing that Remi's primary reaction to being sold as a statue was curiosity about her market value.

## The Archivist's Power and the Erasing of Toadburt

Vostolas the Archivist was discovered crossing names off the guest list in the main hall. He explained that he was not deleting entries but erasing history—people would be able to read about Toadburt but would instantly forget his existence. He offered to accompany the party and document their journey as a 'bedtime story' called 'The Case of the Missing Toad.' Remi was intrigued. Markop was nervous.

The Archivist's room contained imps making posters and flyers. His power to control WHEN Thornbury wrote his field notes (but not WHAT he wrote) suggested a meta-textual authority over the campaign's own documentation. This terrifies Waluigi on a professional level because if an Archivist can decide when records are written, then the historical record itself becomes a managed commodity rather than a neutral account.

Vostolas provided access to Pilo T, a vampire aviation expert who claimed to know where Green T was hiding (in the bathrooms) and promised Remi a ride in a bat-shaped helicopter. Pilo T later lied about the helicopter and tried to push Remi into an oven in the kitchen. Markop stopped him. Waluigi notes that the Shadowfell's hospitality industry maintains a zero percent customer satisfaction rating.

## Marcus Ashford's Poetry and Bowser's Letter

Marcus Ashford, the Iron Legion's military consultant for Orangus Cornelius, represented the Legion's reach through poetry and theft. He swiped Bowser's pink stationery letter to Princess Peach and threatened to read it aloud. The letter, written in surprisingly elegant calligraphy forced upon Bowser by royal tutors, read: 'Dear Peach, I heard you were here. I am NOT kidnapping you. Unless you want to go? No, wait. I am just visiting. Please do not unleash Mario on me. Love, Bowser.'

Ashford taunted the party in verse, calling Bowser a 'former king still roaring loud though he's lost everything' and claiming the Legion had seized his throne 'with elegance and tact.' Bowser demanded to leave. Ashford continued: 'Bowser's strays, what a bore! Run along, run along, mind the door!'

Waluigi recognizes Ashford's method as institutional humiliation—the Legion does not just defeat you; it makes you feel small while doing it. Poetry as a weapon is not new, but using it against a fire-breathing turtle king who could crush you with one hand suggests either extraordinary confidence or extraordinary stupidity. Knowing the Iron Legion, it is probably both.

## Green T's Return and the Portal Plan

Green T resurfaced after the party returned to the manor, explaining he had found portal remains on the second floor that could be activated with the right materials. He had disabled the arcane locks, which did not function well in the Shadeward anyway. He was still upset that Archie had apparently abandoned them by going off with enemy factions.

Green T provided Thornbury's field notebook—an in-progress Mages Guild document describing the initial survey of Raventree Manor by Captain Byscilla Danos and her four-person team. The notebook documented the initials 'OC' and 'AC' appearing throughout the house, the Oracle's work described as 'planar cartography,' and the building's smell of damp stone, old cloth, and something faintly sweet like long-dead incense.

Green T also warned the party not to drink or eat anything the Oracle offered, as it would make them 'impervious'—presumably to something the Oracle wanted them vulnerable to. He explained that dirty work was required: the portal needed ingredients, and using it without being noticed would be the real challenge.

## The Oracle's Manipulation and the Pill

The Oracle sat alone at the dinner table and told Remi privately to sneak a pill to Markop. He offered the same pill to Remi. Markop banged on the door screaming 'DON'T TAKE THE PILL.' The Oracle then offered an apple with something injected into it. Remi denied. Markop burst through the door screaming 'DON'T EAT IT' and found Remi sipping grape juice while the Oracle smiled and said 'it's too late.'

Whether the grape juice was tampered with or whether the Oracle was bluffing remains unclear. Waluigi suspects the Oracle operates on a principle of ambient manipulation: it does not matter whether the specific drink was poisoned if the target spends every subsequent moment wondering whether it was. Waluigi uses this exact tactic in Mario Party. You don't need to steal the star; you just need to make them think you're going to steal the star, and they will sabotage themselves trying to stop you. The Oracle is playing a 50-turn game, and Markop is crying on turn 3.

## Lyranth's Threat and Kyrn's Desperation

Lyranth the Sculptor caught the toads and interrogated them about who killed Vivesna. The toads did not know. She said the ashes traced back to Vivian's blood. She apologized for turning their friends to stone—calling them 'perfect models'—and mentioned that a yellow-suited mustache fellow she had been talking to would be turned to stone next, presumably referring to Wario.

She announced she would prepare something special for the evening's 'actuation,' then left. Kyrn Corvinarus immediately appeared from the shadows and begged the toads for help, explaining that Lyranth planned to turn his friend to stone. The toads said they were weak, dirt poor, and felt their options were limited. They agreed to help for 300 Onyx Blood Vials, noting they could convert the currency later.

## The Peach Loyalist Side Thread

In a separate thread that Waluigi has had to reconstruct from fragmentary reports, Embercap, Dewdrop, and Erick arrived at a location the Rakshasa had specified to pick up items. They found Wario inside, who subsequently stole a Tome of Evil worth 20,000 mushroom coins. A chase ensued: Embercap grabbed Wario's arm in a deadlock, Erick shoulder-bashed Wario into a wall, a mage used Color Spray on Wario's eyes, and Wario turned into a bat and flew away with the tome while everyone missed their swings.

Bryan arrived through a portal at a Mages Guild facility. He found Dan's photograph, confronted Purple T about Archie's whereabouts, and formed an alliance with Dan and a Mages Guild associate to track Archie down. Purple T removed their tracking badges and declared that everything would be on their own terms from now on.

In yet another thread, Mistveil and Big R debriefed a Rakshasa on 'Operation Homecoming,' then accidentally stumbled into a crystal cave containing a dragon discussing plane-merging operations. The dragon mentioned that once the planes merged, 'dragons will rise against them.' They were discovered, lied about what they had seen, and were teleported to Rogueport Bay in the middle of a naval battle between Iron Legion ships, Mushroom Regency ships, and pirates, where Captain Syrup welcomed them.

Waluigi finds the breadth of simultaneous operations occurring across multiple planes, factions, and time zones absolutely staggering. The campaign is not one story. It is at least six stories happening at once, connected by shared characters, shared enemies, and the shared conviction that nothing will get better if anyone stops moving.

## Waluigi's Assessment of the Shadow Estate Campaign

The Shadowfell fragment of the Raventree Crisis is the darkest, most complicated, and most institutionally corrupt theater of the entire dimensional war. Unlike the Feywild, where danger wears flowers and speaks in riddles, the Shadowfell presents danger in its most honest form: bureaucratic, systematic, and dressed in uniforms that claim authority.

The Shadow Anchor's destruction was a victory. Vivian's death was a resolution. The Parallel Dan's exposure was necessary intelligence. But every victory in the Shadowfell came with costs that have not yet been fully calculated. Remi carries a tightening ring she cannot discuss. The real Dan has been indoctrinated into viewing his former allies as enemies. Toadburt has been erased from historical memory by an Archivist who considers forgetting a service. The Mages Guild has drafted Archie into oversight they describe as 'responsibility' but which functions as a leash. And somewhere in the Shadowfell's endless grey landscape, a cult worships Archie Miser as a god based on propaganda texts that describe him as both savior and destroyer.

Waluigi was not in the Shadowfell. Waluigi was in the Feywild being led around by both hands like a kindergartener while a dryad commented on his lack of independence. Waluigi maintains that his experience was equally degrading, if less existentially threatening.

But Waluigi also knows this: the people who survived the Shadow Estate did so by refusing to play by the institution's rules. Green T shot a crystal from the children's table. Bowser bit a vampire bat. Markop whispered a prayer and received an answer. Remi glowed like a disco ball and called it an improvement.

These are not the actions of people who understand what they are doing.

They are the actions of people who refuse to stop doing it.

That is either courage or madness.

Waluigi has stopped trying to tell the difference.

Waluigi is the ultimate judge, jury, and executioner of this historical record. And Waluigi's verdict is that everyone involved is a glorious, incompetent disaster. WAH!

summary: Five years before the assassination of Princess Peach, Professor E. Gadd decided that the linear flow of time was a personal insult to his intellect and built a time machine. Princess Peach, possessing the survival instincts of a lemming, immediately took it for a joyride to the past. She arrived exactly at the moment an extraterrestrial, hyper-militarized race of purple fungal horrors known as the Shroobs invaded the Mushroom Kingdom. What followed was a temporal nightmare involving Time Holes, alien saucers, the harvesting of Toad life-force for fuel, and Mario and Luigi teaming up with their own infant selves. Waluigi watched this unfold, exploited the temporal arbitrage for massive financial gain, and observed how the early predecessor of the Regal Empire used crashed Shroob technology to jumpstart their modern Magitek arsenal. The crisis was eventually resolved when the heroes realized the 'power source' they were collecting was actually the cage for the ultimate alien threat, and they defeated an intergalactic armada using the chemical composition of BABY TEARS. Waluigi considers this the single most embarrassing, logically offensive, and strategically absurd sequence of events in the history of the Doughnut World. He is documenting it here because the Mages' Guild tried to memory-wipe the continent, and Waluigi refuses to let Mario get away with weaponizing toddlers. WAH.
description:
Waluigi must state for the historical record: Chronomancy is not a science. It is an ego trip for wizards who are too lazy to wait for Thursday. 

Before Waluigi dives into the multi-layered catastrophe of the Shroob Temporal Incursion, context must be established. The year was 950 BF. Princess Peach was alive, the Mushroom Kingdom was prospering in the North-West, and the political landscape was stable. It was a time of peace, which meant it was incredibly boring, which meant someone was bound to build a doomsday device out of sheer intellectual boredom.

That someone was Professor Elvin Gadd. 

E. Gadd is a genius in the same way that a tornado is a landscaper. He creates things of immense power with absolutely zero regard for the structural integrity of reality. He built a Time Machine. He did not build safety protocols. He did not build a temporal tether. He built a machine, powered it with a mysterious, glowing artifact called the Cobalt Star, and said, 'Let's see what happens!'

Princess Peach, accompanied by Toadiko and Toadbert (who are essentially professional victims), volunteered to take the maiden voyage back to the year 840 BF—the dawn of the Mushroom Kingdom's Golden Age. 

She did not return. The Time Machine returned empty, battered, and occupied by a hostile alien creature. And thus, the worst week of Waluigi's life—and the secret origin of the Regal Empire's technological supremacy—began.

## The Geopolitical Board: 840 BF vs 950 BF

To understand the absolute mess the Mario brothers stepped into, one must understand the geography and politics of the Doughnut World in the year 840 BF.

In the North-West, the Mushroom Kingdom was just entering its Golden Age. Peach's royal ancestors were establishing the cheerful, pastel-colored, aggressively optimistic society that Waluigi finds so deeply nauseating. They were peaceful. They were unprepared. They had no standing army capable of repelling an intergalactic threat.

However, to the South and East, a different power was coalescing. The 'Proto-Regal Empire'—a highly disciplined, militaristic federation of human warlords modeling themselves after ancient Roman legions—was rapidly expanding its borders. They were building fortresses, establishing the first iterations of what would become the 'Beige Brigade,' and imposing strict order on the chaotic post-cataclysm world.

When the Shroobs attacked in 840 BF, they didn't just attack the Mushroom Kingdom. They attacked the entire continent. 

The Shroobs were an invasive species from a dying planet. They were purple (which Waluigi admits is a magnificent color choice, though they ruined it with their terrible fashion sense), fungal in nature, and spoke a language that sounded like a barcode scanner malfunctioning. They possessed flying saucers, laser weaponry, genetic modification technology, and a complete absence of empathy. 

When Peach's Time Machine arrived in 840 BF, it materialized directly into the Vanguard of the Shroob invasion force, led by Princess Shroob. Peach, displaying a rare moment of tactical awareness, used the Cobalt Star to trap Princess Shroob's older sister—the Elder Princess Shroob—shattering the star into fragments to seal the prison. 

This act of desperation saved the past from immediate annihilation, but scattered the Cobalt Shards across the continent, creating a network of 'Time Holes'—chronal ruptures linking 840 BF directly to 950 BF.

## The Plumber Paradox: Enter the Babies

With Time Holes opening up across the modern Mushroom Kingdom, Mario and Luigi did what they always do: they jumped into the nearest gaping anomaly without a risk assessment or a safety harness. 

They emerged in the past, specifically in the village of Hollijolli, which was currently being glassed by Shroob UFOs. And who did they find waiting for them? 

Their infant selves. Baby Mario and Baby Luigi.

Waluigi needs to pause here. Waluigi needs to take a deep, cleansing breath. 

Let us analyze the tactical, ethical, and temporal implications of taking YOUR OWN INFANT SELF INTO A LIVE COMBAT ZONE. 

If Baby Mario dies, Adult Mario ceases to exist. This is basic temporal mechanics. It is the grandfather paradox stripped down to its most immediate, suicidal components. A logical, sane individual would have immediately evacuated the infants to a secure bunker in the present, sealed the door, and gone back to fight the aliens alone. 

What did Mario do? He handed Baby Mario a HAMMER. He strapped the infant to his back, used him as a projectile weapon, and actively encouraged a toddler to engage in melee combat against heavily armed extraterrestrial shock troops. 

Waluigi has been accused of many crimes. Waluigi has been called a thief, a cheat, a scoundrel, and a menace. But Waluigi has NEVER weaponized a preschooler to solve a geopolitical crisis. The sheer, breathtaking irresponsibility of the Mario brothers is a stain on the history of the Mushroom Kingdom. They treated the space-time continuum like a playground and their own past selves like disposable power-ups.

## The Vim Economy: Shroob Logistics

While the plumbers were busy committing chronological child abuse, Waluigi was analyzing the enemy. The Shroobs were not mindless beasts. They were a highly structured, terrifyingly efficient military industrial complex. 

Their primary resource was 'Vim'—the life energy of Toads. The Shroobs didn't just kill the local population; they harvested them. They converted Toad Town into a dystopian processing plant. They genetically modified local flora (creating monstrous entities like Petey Piranha's corrupted ancestors) and pumped Vim into their saucers to fuel their war machine. 

Waluigi secretly observed a Shroob Vim Factory operating in a corrupted forest known as Toadwood. The efficiency was staggering. Toads were strapped to trees, their vitality drained through biomechanical roots, refined into glowing green liquid, and shipped to the Shroob mothership. 

It was horrific. It was monstrous. But from a purely administrative standpoint? It was brilliant logistics. 

Waluigi notes a chilling historical parallel here. Look at the Iron Legion in the current era (1040 BF). Look at their 'Imperial Processing Facilities.' Look at how they catalogue, process, and extract utility from prisoners of war with cold, bureaucratic efficiency. 

Waluigi has a theory—a theory that the Mages' Guild will deny until their dying breath. The Iron Legion didn't invent their processing methodology from scratch. They learned it. Where did they learn it? From the remnants of Shroob data-cores left behind in 840 BF. The Shroobs were defeated, but their logistics manuals survived. The Iron Legion is just the Shroob invasion painted grey and taught how to file taxes.

## The Proto-Imperial Response: Scavenging the Future

While the Mushroom Kingdom was being turned into a Vim farm, the Proto-Regal Empire to the East was mounting a very different response to the Shroob threat.

The early Imperial Legions did not have magic hammers or legendary jumping abilities. They had discipline, spears, and a burgeoning understanding of early techno-magic (Aurean legacy tech). When Shroob saucers began probing their borders, the Proto-Empire did not panic. They formed shield walls. They died by the thousands. But they held the line.

During one of his own temporal excursions (which Waluigi will detail shortly), Waluigi witnessed an engagement at the edge of the Thwomp Volcano. A Shroob command saucer was shot down by a coordinated volley of massive, enchanted ballista bolts fired by a Proto-Imperial cohort. 

The Legionnaires did not cheer. They did not celebrate. They immediately cordoned off the crash site, executed the surviving Shroob pilots with clinical precision, and brought in teams of scholars to dismantle the saucer.

This is the secret history of the Regal Empire. Their modern Magitek? Their energy rifles, their floating fortresses, their 'Protocol Umbra' containment fields? It is all reverse-engineered Shroob technology. The Empire's obsession with 'Order' and suppressing chaos was born in the fires of 840 BF, when they looked up at the sky, saw purple fungal aliens trying to harvest their souls, and collectively decided: *We must build a cage strong enough to hold the stars themselves.*

The Mario brothers fought the Shroobs. The Regal Empire *studied* them. Guess which faction currently rules the Midlands?

## Waluigi’s Temporal Arbitrage (Or, How to Profit from a Paradox)

Waluigi did not sit idly by while the space-time continuum collapsed. Waluigi saw opportunity. 

Professor E. Gadd’s lab in the present (950 BF) was littered with active Time Holes. With the Mario brothers distracted in the past, Waluigi slipped into the lab and began his own temporal operations. 

Waluigi realized that with access to both 840 BF and 950 BF, he could engage in the ultimate form of insider trading. He could bury a cheap, useless antique in the past, travel to the present, dig it up, and sell it as a priceless historical artifact. He could observe which land tracts became valuable real estate in 950 BF, travel back to 840 BF, and purchase the deeds for pennies using era-appropriate currency stolen from Shroob-occupied vaults.

It was foolproof. It was elegant. It was the greatest financial scheme in the history of the Doughnut World.

There was only one problem: Wario.

Waluigi arrived at a designated burial site in 840 BF, carrying a chest of soon-to-be-vintage coins, only to find an infant with a yellow cap and a zig-zag mustache already digging in the dirt. 

Baby Wario.

Even as a toddler, the man was a greedy, intolerable nuisance. Baby Wario had somehow sniffed out Waluigi's buried treasure, dug it up, and was currently attempting to eat a gold coin. 

Waluigi attempted to reason with the infant. 'Listen, you garlic-scented gremlin, that is MY investment portfolio maturing over a century.' 

Baby Wario responded by throwing a magnet at Waluigi's face and waddling away with the chest at a speed that defied infant biomechanics. Waluigi spent three days in 840 BF chasing a toddler across a lava-filled cavern to retrieve his own money. The indignity of the situation still causes Waluigi's blood pressure to spike. 

This is the tragedy of time travel. You think you are mastering the cosmos, and you end up getting mugged by your business partner's diaper-wearing past self.

## The Cobalt Star Idiocy: The Worst Fetch Quest in History

While Waluigi was dealing with financial setbacks, the Mario brothers were engaging in a quest of such profound, staggering stupidity that it belongs in a textbook on how NOT to save the world.

The premise was simple: E. Gadd's time machine needed the Cobalt Star to function. The star had been shattered into pieces by Princess Peach when she arrived in the past. E. Gadd communicated through a briefcase-radio (which Waluigi admits was a neat piece of tech) and told the brothers to find the shards to fix the machine and rescue the Princess.

Let us review the facts. 

Princess Peach, trapped in the past, surrounded by aliens, deliberately shattered her only ticket home. Why would she do this? Because, as previously mentioned, she used the Cobalt Star to TRAP the Elder Princess Shroob—the true, world-ending leader of the alien armada. The shards of the star were the bars of the cage.

Therefore, by collecting the shards and putting them back together, the Mario brothers were actively REASSEMBLING THE CAGE OF THE APOCALYPSE. 

Did they question this? No. Did E. Gadd—a supposed genius—consider why the star was broken? No. They just saw shiny pieces of glass and started gluing them together because a glowing objective marker told them to. 

Every time they found a shard, the Elder Princess Shroob's spirit grew stronger. Every time they defeated a Shroob commander (like the monstrous Swiggler or the Shrooboid Brat), they patted themselves on the back, oblivious to the fact that they were doing the enemy's work for them. 

Waluigi watched this from afar and nearly wept with frustration. It is agonizing to be a genius surrounded by people whose primary problem-solving methodology is 'jump on it until it yields a collectible.'

## The Climax: Shroob Castle and the Great Betrayal

The final confrontation took place in Shroob Castle—which was just Princess Peach's castle, conquered and remodeled by the Shroobs with an aesthetic that Waluigi can only describe as 'Gothic Fungus.' 

The Mario brothers, carrying the nearly complete Cobalt Star and an abducted Princess Peach (who had a Shroob mushroom clamped to her face, a look that honestly improved her conversational skills), breached the throne room to confront Princess Shroob.

Princess Shroob was formidable. She floated on a mechanized throne, fired energy beams, and commanded a personal guard. But she was ultimately defeated by four plumbers swinging hammers in synchronized, physics-defying combat rhythms. 

And then, the inevitable happened.

The final shard of the Cobalt Star was united with the rest. The star was complete. And immediately, the Elder Princess Shroob was released from her prison.

The Elder Princess was a nightmare. A massive, multi-tentacled, crown-wearing abomination that radiated dark energy. She immediately betrayed her younger sister, absorbed the remaining Shroob forces, and initiated a battle that threatened to collapse the timeline itself.

This was the moment. The climax of the temporal war. The fate of the past and the future hung in the balance. How was this terrifying, intergalactic, time-traveling horror defeated?

## The Baby Tear Resolution: An Insult to Science and Magic

Waluigi is going to type this next sentence very slowly, because every keystroke fills him with white-hot rage.

The Shroob armada, the Elder Princess Shroob, and the entire alien bio-weapon infrastructure were defeated because BABY TEARS happen to contain a chemical compound that is lethally toxic to Shroob biology.

Baby. Tears.

Not a superweapon. Not a localized temporal collapse. Not a masterstroke of arcane engineering. The tears of crying infants.

Let us break down the utter absurdity of this resolution.

Throughout the entire adventure, the Shroobs had conquered continents, enslaved populations, built flying fortresses, and mastered chronomancy. They were apex predators. And their fatal, species-wide weakness was the saline solution produced by the lachrymal glands of human toddlers.

When Baby Luigi started crying (because he is weak and pathetic, unlike Baby Waluigi, who never cried, only demanded better service), his tears splashed onto a Shroob mushroom, instantly dissolving it. E. Gadd, witnessing this through his radio, realized the truth. He used his Hydrogush 4000 system to mass-produce a chemical equivalent of Baby Luigi's tears, pumped it through the Time Holes, and rained it down upon the past.

The 'Tear Rain' melted the Shroob saucers. It dissolved their armor. It washed away the purple fungal corruption that had choked the Mushroom Kingdom. 

It was a Deus Ex Machina of such breathtaking laziness that Waluigi almost threw himself into a Time Hole just to avoid witnessing it. It invalidates all military strategy. It insults the discipline of the Mages' Guild. It makes a mockery of the Proto-Regal Empire's sacrifices. 

'How did you defeat the alien armada, Mario?' 
'Oh, my infant brother threw a tantrum and we weaponized his sadness.'

It is DISGUSTING. It is NARRATIVE CHEATING. And worst of all, Mario got a parade for it.

## The Aftermath: Erasure and the Birth of Paranoia

When the dust settled and the Shroobs were melted into puddles of crying-induced goo, the heroes returned to 950 BF. 

What happened next is the reason most people in the Doughnut World do not know about the Shroob Temporal Incursion.

E. Gadd, realizing the catastrophic damage that widespread knowledge of time travel and alien invasions would cause, deployed a memory-wiping device. He claimed it was to 'preserve the timeline' and 'prevent paradoxes.' 

Waluigi knows the truth. The memory wipe was orchestrated by Toadsworth the Elder and the Mages' Guild. 

The Guild realized that E. Gadd's time machine was too dangerous to exist. The Proto-Regal Empire (which was rapidly becoming the modern Regal Empire) had secured enough Shroob technology in the past to guarantee their future dominance, and they did not want anyone going back to contest their salvage claims. 

So, a mass memory modification was deployed across the Mushroom Kingdom. The public forgot the purple skies. They forgot the saucers. They forgot the Vim factories.

But you cannot entirely erase trauma.

The Shroob invasion happened in 840 BF, at the start of the Golden Age. The people of the Mushroom Kingdom forgot the details, but their collective unconscious remembered the fear. They remembered that the sky could open up and rain death. They remembered that their peace was fragile.

This subconscious trauma festered for centuries. It bred a subtle, pervasive paranoia in the Mushroom Kingdom's leadership. It made them fearful of external threats, fearful of the Mages' Guild, fearful of the rising Regal Empire. 

And in 950 BF, when the heroes returned and their memories were wiped, that paranoia accelerated. 

Waluigi posits a direct, undeniable line between the Shroob Temporal Incursion in 950 BF and the Assassination of Princess Peach in 955 BF. 

Toadsworth the Elder lived through the Shroob crisis. He saw the Princess recklessly endanger the timeline. He saw the incompetence of the heroes. He saw the power of the Regal Empire's scavenged tech. The memory wipe might have clouded his conscious mind, but the terror remained.

When the conspirators approached Toadsworth Sr. five years later with 'the arrangement' to eliminate Princess Peach, he didn't just agree out of ambition. He agreed out of FEAR. He believed the Princess was a destabilizing element. He believed her chaotic, adventure-seeking nature (like jumping into untested time machines) would eventually doom the kingdom. He enabled her assassination because the trauma of the Shroob invasion taught him that 'Order'—the kind of order the Regal Empire was building—was the only way to survive.

## Waluigi's Final Assessment

The Shroob Temporal Incursion is the hidden hinge upon which the modern history of the Doughnut World turns.

It gave the Regal Empire their Magitek. It traumatized the Mushroom Kingdom's leadership, laying the psychological groundwork for Peach's assassination. It proved that the Mages' Guild is willing to overwrite the minds of an entire populace to maintain control.

And it proved, once and for all, that Mario and Luigi are not tactical geniuses. They are incredibly lucky buffoons who bumble their way through apocalyptic threats, relying on magic stars, time travel, and the chemical composition of toddler tears to save them from their own catastrophic decisions.

Waluigi remembers. Waluigi kept his notes hidden in a lead-lined, chronal-dampened safe. The Mages' Guild could not wipe a mind as magnificent and impenetrable as Waluigi's.

Waluigi knows the truth. The heroes are frauds. The Empire is built on stolen alien scrap. The kingdom's golden age was a lie maintained by amnesia. 

And somewhere, in the deep temporal vaults of E. Gadd's lab, the time machine still sits. Waiting. 

Waluigi might just have to borrow it one day. Not to save the world. But to go back to 840 BF, find Baby Wario, and dropkick him into a volcano before he can steal Waluigi's investment portfolio.

WAH.

summary: This sequence of events perfectly encapsulates why Waluigi despises the Mages' Guild AND the Iron Legion. Archie Miser, recovering from being repeatedly knocked unconscious, was approached by a Guild 'doctor' named Parson Pellinost. The doctor healed him, announced Archie was now in his debt, and when Archie demanded a refund, the doctor LITERALLY RIPPED THE HEALING MAGIC BACK OUT OF HIS BODY. Waluigi must admit: that is an incredibly stylish scam. Simultaneously, the Legion claimed Bones was suffering from 'Starlight Fever,' a fake magical disease, when in reality they had pumped him full of sedatives to keep him in a medically induced coma. The level of institutional gaslighting is staggering, but their operational security is pathetic.
description:
Waluigi must break this down into its component failures, because the sheer density of incompetence and malice requires a masterclass in analysis.

## The Repossessed Heal (Parson Pellinost's Hustle)

Archie was resting. A man named Parson Pellinost—claiming to be a Mages' Guild doctor—breezed past the magical wards, produced a crumpled medical card, and healed Archie. 

'You are now in my debt,' Pellinost declared.

Archie, possessing the financial instincts of a man who already owes 2,062 gold pieces for a broken rope, demanded a 'refund.' 

Waluigi wants everyone to pause and appreciate the sheer, unadulterated PETTINESS of what happened next. Parson Pellinost did not argue. He did not file a grievance. He simply reached out and FORCEFULLY DRAINED THE HEALING MAGIC BACK OUT OF ARCHIE'S BODY. Archie immediately felt terrible again. Pellinost told him to 'use his card if he needed him' and walked away.

Waluigi hates the Mages' Guild. Waluigi despises their bureaucracy. But Waluigi respects a good grift. Healing someone, establishing a debt, and literally *repo'ing their health* when they complain is a level of aggressive capitalism that brings a tear to Waluigi's eye. Wario would be taking notes.

## The Manifestation of Agony

Following the medical extortion, Darno Spriggon (the man with the stolen Legion ring) offered to 'show Archie a monster.' Archie immediately saw a giant fireball monster that no one else could see. It chased him upstairs.

Let Waluigi translate this for the layperson: The Guild/Legion alliance deployed targeted, localized psychological warfare against Archie. They manifested his 'pure agony' into an illusion visible only to him, designed to isolate him from the group. It worked flawlessly because Archie's default response to psychological trauma is to run away and lock himself in a dark room.

## The Oracle's Intervention and the 'Starlight' Fraud

Inside the locked room, the Oracle appeared, healed Archie (presumably without charging him interest), and dropped a massive piece of intelligence: The Mages' Guild plans to use Archie's research and his 'entropy-bleeding' magical signature to establish interdimensional travel on demand. Archie is not a prisoner; he is a BATTERY.

Before they could process this, Iron Legion guards breached the room to detain the Oracle. Archie tried to negotiate. During the standoff, they noticed Bones, asleep in a bed, having not woken up in hours.

The Legion guards claimed Bones was suffering from 'Starlight Fever'—a magical malady causing uncontrollable surges. The Oracle immediately called them liars, stating Starlight Fever doesn't affect Toads.

Archie then managed to steal/read a Legion tablet. Waluigi has reviewed the transcript of this tablet, and it is a masterpiece of bureaucratic evil:

**FALSIFIED DIAGNOSIS:** *Starlight Fever.* (Note: Zero arcane surge activity detected. Diagnosis does not match patient presentation.)
**ACTUAL DIAGNOSIS:** *Somnium Captivus — Induced Arcane Coma via Compound Sedation.* (Deliberate administration of a dual-layer mundane/arcane sedative. Unlawful detainment under Article 9.)

The Iron Legion wasn't treating Bones. They had chemically and magically lobotomized him to keep him quiet after he successfully infiltrated Aegis Command. They filed the real diagnosis right beneath the fake one on the same tablet, because the Iron Legion's obsession with accurate paperwork completely overrides their instinct for a cover-up.

Waluigi is offended. If you are going to drug a political prisoner and lie about it, KEEP TWO SEPARATE LEDGERS. Amateurs. WAH.

summary: To escape the Iron Legion, the Oracle snapped his fingers and teleported Archie and the comatose Bones to the 'Planar Sanctum.' It began as a beautiful, star-lit library and immediately devolved into a cosmic slaughterhouse. The floor shattered to reveal two massive Crystal Tethers (one Umbral Violet, one Volatile Orange) literally tearing a man apart in a metal tank. A detached room revealed glass vats filled with malformed, weeping, tube-fed humanoids suspended in luminescent fluid. The Oracle revealed this is the fate awaiting them if the timelines aren't severed. Waluigi has strong stomach for villainy, but this crosses the line from 'scheming' into 'existential body horror.'
description:
Waluigi has maintained throughout this encyclopedia that the Iron Legion and the Mages' Guild are corrupt. But corruption usually means taking bribes or falsifying documents. The Planar Sanctum proves that their corruption is metaphysical. They are quite literally mining human suffering to manipulate the fabric of reality.

## The Library of the Void

The initial arrival point was deceptive. A circular chamber with elaborately carved wooden shelves extending upward like stacked bands. Three grand lecterns in the center holding ornate, locked tomes. And directly overhead, a tiny aperture revealing a swirling starscape. 

Waluigi appreciates a good library. Knowledge is power, and power is leverage. Archie found a torn-out page referencing *Arcane Tethers, Planar Threading, Planar Resonance, Quintessence, The Weight of Time,* and *Accretion Sites.* This confirms that the Guild isn't just studying the Planar Fracture; they are actively trying to HARNESS it. They are treating the collapse of reality as a public transit project.

## The Grisly Tableau: The Tethers

The illusion of scholarly tranquility ended when the floor shattered like fine china, ripping the royal purple carpet apart. (Waluigi takes personal offense to the destruction of royal purple carpet. Barbarians.)

Beneath the floor lay a grand central chamber open to the starfield. Two massive crystal formations were mounted in metallic casings:
- **The Western Crystal:** Thrumming with umbral violet energy.
- **The Eastern Crystal:** Flashing erratically with volatile orange energy.

These are the **Crystal Tethers**. And in the exact center between them lay a cracked metal tank. Behind the tank stood a man, silhouetted by lightning, enveloped by grasping tendrils of energy that seemed to rip and tear at him from both sides. 

Archie, demonstrating his usual lack of situational awareness, put his hand on the case and called it 'beautiful.' The Oracle corrected him. This is the agony that the Corvinarus curse inflicts. This man (likely a key figure of the bloodline, perhaps the original Orangus Cornelius or the architect of 'The Grafting') is acting as the living battery for the dimensional rift. Twenty years of agony to keep the planes tethered together.

## The Flesh Vats

If the Tethers were tragic, the adjacent room was an atrocity. 

A detached circular chamber drifting with centrifugal entropy. Inside were large glass tanks connected by thick pipes. Suspended within a glowing, luminescent fluid were humanoid bodies. 

They were malformed. Flesh open with weeping sores. Limbs ending prematurely. Metal tubes impaling their flesh and extending down their open mouths. Their eyes were open, but it was impossible to tell if they were alive. A disposal chute nearby indicated what happened to the 'failed' experiments.

This is what the Iron Legion and Mages' Guild are doing behind closed doors. They are not just treating prisoners as logistics; they are treating them as raw biological material for dimensional stabilization. The 'Somnium Captivus' that Bones is currently suffering from? It is likely the precursor to ending up in one of these tubes. 

The Oracle made it explicit: *'If we do the ritual, we won't have to end up in a vat like this.'*

## Waluigi's Assessment

The Planar Sanctum is the dark heart of the Raventree Crisis. It proves that the overlapping dimensions are not just a magical accident; they are being actively, artificially sustained through horrific biological and arcane machinery. 

The Violet energy likely corresponds to the Shadowfell (Shadow Estate). The Orange energy likely corresponds to the Feywild (Overgrown Manor, the 'Orange Alignment' involving Hjumpik). The man in the middle is the anchor.

Waluigi has stolen from museums. Waluigi has rigged go-kart races. Waluigi has even scammed desperate Toads with useless corsets during a biological pandemic. But Waluigi has NEVER put a sentient being in a flesh vat to harvest their soul for a dimensional subway system. 

There is evil, and then there is *this*. The Iron Legion and the Mages' Guild must be dismantled. Not because Waluigi is a hero. But because Waluigi refuses to live in a universe where the ultimate authority is this utterly devoid of style and basic decency.

WAH.
